body: We visited Brief Garden today, a fantastic beautiful garden with lots of art. We enjoyed the beautiful statues and landscaped gardens. You could see the garden for yourself and at the house the guide would be there again. The house was beautiful too. There was a lot of art and a lot was told about it. The owner Bewis Bawa was very rich and knew many people from nobility: Sir Laurens Olivier, Lord Mountbatten, Prince Edward and also many famous actresses. There was some art with text in it about Bevis Bawa and it became clear that he was not an easy man. If he rang his bell and his staff didn't come straight away, he could go on a rampage. Then we suddenly saw a work of art that said: Incest is nice! The guide said that he was a pedophile who abused young boys and that everyone knew about it. Disgusting! It gave a very bad aftertaste to our visit
title: What a bad aftertaste, he's a pedophile!

body: I am totally dissatisfied with my recent visit to Brief Garden in Beruwala last week.The experience was extremely disappointing and fell far below acceptable standards. Despite paying an entrance fee of LKR 500 per person and an additional LKR 50,000 for a photoshoot, the overall service and management were highly unprofessional.Firstly, the conduct of your housekeeping staff member, Ananda, was completely unacceptable. He displayed rude and disrespectful behavior towards my family. At one point, when a family member unknowingly entered the house area, he shouted at them in a manner that was both humiliating and inappropriate. Such behavior is inexcusable, especially in a place that welcomes paying visitors.Secondly, the garden itself was not properly maintained, which further added to our disappointment. The greenery was totally gone due to dry weather where they do not water the plants properly.Moreover, there was a clear lack of communication and mismanagement regarding photography guidelines. Prior to our visit, we contacted your team to clarify details, yet we were not informed of any restrictions concerning photography in the house area. It was only after arriving at the location that these rules were abruptly communicated by your staff. This lack of transparency is highly unprofessional.We traveled all the way from Colombo with clear expectations based on the information provided to us. Unfortunately, the experience did not justify the time, effort, or money spent.More importantly, the treatment we received was unfair. While standard pricing indicates LKR 500 for garden entry and LKR 2,000 for house access, we were denied entry to the house despite paying a significantly higher total amount. Meanwhile, foreign visitors were allowed inside. This inconsistency raises serious concerns about discriminatory practices.Overall, this experience did not justify the time, money, or effort spent. Immediate improvements in staff behavior, transparency, and fair treatment are necessary.I would never ever recommend this place to anyone.
title: Total dissapointment and a total rip off Money. Never go to place

body: It is worth visiting this very quiet garden area.
title: Very nice complex with great garden

body: One of my highlights of this trip. Many small paths run through this paradise, laid out with great attention to detail! Many sculptures, tropical plants and the deceased owner's and artist's worth seeing home are worth a visit!
title: Enchanted dream garden

body: This is interesting a bit more expensive than we thought (3000) our tuk tuk driver was able to point out things like a guide. We unexpectedly realised the art gallery part was a homo-erotic exhibition which was fine but the life of Bevis Bawa as you start to piece it together revealed a man with an infatuation with local boys and one artwork depicts the writing ‘incest is best’. So go with an open mind.
title: A bit of a surprise-Brief Garden and the life of Bevis

body: Lovely wild gardens with interesting history. So peaceful, feels like you’re immersed in nature. Surround by beautiful tropical plants, you can’t help but feel like you’re in the Amazon rainforest!
title: Peaceful tropical garden

body: We were very disappointed with our visit to Brief Garden in Kalutara. From the moment we arrived, the welcome was downright unpleasant – no warmth, no consideration, it honestly felt like we were bothering them.The entrance fee is overpriced (€10 per person) for what you get. The garden itself is pleasant, but the visit is completely self-guided, with no explanations, no guide, no brochure, and no informational signs. Nothing is done to highlight the history or value of the place.It’s a shame, because the location has potential, but the staff’s attitude and the total lack of effort to inform or welcome visitors completely ruin the experience.I do not recommend it.
title: Very disappointing – not worth it!

body: Are any of guys waiting to visit this place? Don't even think about it. It's so damn terrible. I'm disgusted. It's nothing like the photos. Don't even think to take your family here. Ticket cost is also too high. My cousin's garden is better than this. But u can take some photos though.
title: Don't visit this place

body: A little out of the way from anywhere but reachable by Tuk Tuk. This is not an amazing garden. More average, with plenty of greenery, mostly bamboo and grass. There's a nice house with old relics and an informative guide. I feel the whole experience will take most people less than an hour, for the entrance price of 3,000 ruppee each we weren't blown away.
title: To expensive

body: House and gardens are lovely. Best visited in the morning as tours arrive mid morning. Interesting plants and superb house and gardens lots of erotic art
title: Erotic artworks and beautiful gardens

body: A wonderful garden with exquisite interior designs in nature. Do not miss to spend some time to feel and experience the mastery of integrating nature into a dwelling house.Also do not miss the blue door…
title: Where Taste and Mastery Meets

body: Not worth if you dont have any interst in archietecture dont go there its not worth and is costly and not worth. ...........
title: Not worth

body: I don't get what a lot the fuss is about.Apart from the garden/lawn at the top by the house the garden is really a track through some random bush.No indications about the plants or anything. In a couple of places it looks like it could have been a nice place to spend some time but that day is long past due to nature taking over.The house has the guided tour, many old paintings and a bit about the original owner.3000 rupees per person (foreigners) was a bit steep.Been there, seen that and wouldn't waste any more time.
title: Average at best

body: After visiting lunuganga we went to see the Garden of Bevis Bawa. The brief garden is more compact and u can freely walk around only inside the house is someone guiding. Both lunuganga and brief are worth visiting. There not comparable both unique in there own way.
title: Compact garden of Eden

body: The Gardens were amazing and well manicured and we enjoyed the the house and the life style of the original owner Bevis Bawa
title: Brief the home and garden of Bevis and Bawa

body: An amazing escape by landscape architect Bevis Bawa, the Brief Garden lies tucked in a scenic corner of Bentota. Such a beautifully planned and landscaped garden with wonderful water ponds and water bodies created in unusual shapes and green ups and downs, surrounding the lovely house that is ensconced in the greenery. The house interior of Bevis Bawa is again lovely architecturally and has on display a large number of paintings by him as well as other famous artists. There are photographs of the renowned people he hosted as well.With a lot of history narrated by one of the housekeepers, it made for a good visit. The current owners are requested to contribute more towards the upkeep of the gardens as that would really add to the beauty of the property. All in all a visit worth indulging in while in Bentota.
title: Outrageously beautiful

body: What a Little Gem. Its tucked away and best to go by Tuk Tuk as the road leading to it narrow & a little bumpy, but all good fun. Worth a trip.
title: Lovely Gardens

body: Small but interesting garden, with chance to look around the bungalow as well. We were only there about an hour. Take mosquito spray
title: Small but good for a quick visit

body: A wonderful place, half an hour's drive by Tuk Tuk. The tickets were outrageously expensive (only minus). The garden is an architectural gem of a landscape and, together with the beautiful house, gives an insight into the decadent artistic life that Bewa lived here. There are pictures of Queen Ingrid, who allegedly visited the place several times. It can be argued that the water basins in particular could be better maintained, but in a way the slow decay suits the place. Remember to leave the tuk tuk waiting. It is so remote that no one comes by.
title: Beautiful place

body: The guide is rude to Sri Lankans. Even though we paid Rs. 2000 for the house and garden, the moment we stepped into the house he shouted across the hall that we had only paid for the garden. Even after showing the ticket the guide did not apologize. Complained to the Manager who made a weak apology and excused the guide because he was "busy". It's obvious they have no regard for locals. Note other reviewers also mention this rudeness.
title: Avoid the place

body: A rustic journey through a jungle-like forest. We found the garden interesting and were lucky enough to have many things explained to us in the house.We enjoyed the visit.
title: Beautiful old garden with attached house and interesting history

body: Breif Garden, Bevis Bawa's home, is truly one of a kind. It feels like a scene from a movie with its stunning landscape and unbelievable architecture. This place stays with you, an unforgettable experience that's impossible to forget.
title: Unforgettable!!

body: Sorry very disappointed with it all, not much colour in the whole place….guide, wasn’t interested in people coming there. Only 1 sign….find it yourself…3/4 hour done….no refreshments
title: Brief gardens

body: A beautifully well maintained garden, must visit. Surrounded by trees and flower plants, a great place to escape from busy city.
title: forestry vibe

body: I am fascinated by the works of the Bawa brothers and am glad I came by to see this place. If you too are a fan and have read all about either or both, this is worth the visit. The whole experience is not for all, especially if you are expecting a whimsical, well-kept garden. The outer areas are wild and free, which is what I expected, and not manicured. If are on your own, you may get a little intimidated going around, since you don’t know where you are going. (employee just takes your money and have you enter the gate). However, wherever that may be, in the end, you do end up back at the house.The house, its closer grounds, wonderful to frolic around. I do recommend wearing good ol' sneakers if you plan to really explore the whole place. Also yes, do bring bug spray.I really wish this place all the best, as it represents the “renowned horticulturalists and landscaper”. One way to start is by being consistent, improve staff and product skills. Overall the right attitude is still key.
title: Bawa fan, happy, almost.

body: A hidden gem - loved it! Beautiful garden and house with lots of interest - a lot of architectural thought and a lifetime's work have gone into it. I love the fact that the house and garden was left to the Head Gardener on Bevis Bawa's death. A labour of love. I love the fact that so many Hollywood stars from the 40s/50s came and stayed there - the parties they must have had! Very interesting way to spend a couple of hours if you are in the Bentota area.
title: Gem of a garden

body: We took a tuk tuk ride out to brief gardens. We rang the bell to be let in and wandered around the beautiful gardens up to the main house, where we were met by our guide who took us on an interesting tour, explaining all the art work and the smaller court yard areas of the house. Well worth a visit a hidden gem!
title: Mum and three daughters from England

body: I loved it here. An amazing variety of plants and beautiful gardens to wander around which took well over 90 minutes to see properly. Then a little tour inside the house where the guide had a really good knowledge of the many decorative items there. A very interesting visit. Cost 2,000 rupees - a bargain. Take mosquito repellant!
title: Beautiful gardens

body: A hidden gem, that should not be missed by anyone interested in gardening/plants or nature. It is amazingly beautiful, with a mixture of tropical forest/park and a European style garden, plus the house itself. The forest setting also meant bird song. We were unable to stay for the tea and cakes available at the main house, but that would have made a very nice conclusion. Surprised that not all reviewers give it top marks, but as for all gardens one aspect could be the time of the year of the visit. In early February it was certainly wonderful. Photos show that among house guests in the past were both Edward VII, Vivien Leigh and Laurence Olivier.
title: Must for nature lovers

body: While the garden itself was worth exploring to enjoy the different fauna and flora and innovative landscspe, our experience was soured by the 2 men who were in charge of the premises. One person by the name of Ananda and another fellow who appeared to be his assistant. We had paid the local rate of Rs 500 each for the garden tour and had no intention of visiting the interior of the house. But the moment we stepped up the stairs leading to the perimeter of the house, these 2 fellows came out and quite rudely literally chased us off saying garden is below the stairs. We have seen plenty of beautiful houses during our travels and had no intention of surreptitiously stepping inside the house as if we have never seen one! They seem not to be aware of the difference betwen the interior and exterior of a house. This is not the way to treat visitors and Ananda especially comes off as quite rude and aloof to both local and foreign visitors alike. He does not possess the usual Sri Lankan hospitality and needs to be given a good lesson in PR. We did not notice him even once smiling and being accomodating towards guests. Also suggest to install a board saying garden only visitors not allowed up the stairs! Lunuganga was a much more wholesome experience as opposed to this.
title: Experience spoiled by rude staff

body: Very good place to chill, nice food, nice environment and Arun kc part of the bar staff is very friendly and professionnal ! Do not hesitate to go there !!
title: Very good experience

body: Decent, definitely not worth the trek or price (2k per head) I think the garden is worth 1k! Bring some mosquito repellent if you’re wearing shorts 🤙🏼
title: Meh

body: Brief garden is located in Beruwala,Kalutara District.This garden was created by Bevis Bawa, the brother of renowned architect Jefri Bawa. There are more than 100 species of trees spread over an area of about 20 acres.This is very popular as a beautiful garden that is appealing to both young and old.
title: Brief Garden by Bevis Bawa

body: A highlight of our trip! Really beautiful garden + accessible garden with winding paths that all lead to the main house. The house is still lived in by the head gardener/landscaper and took afternoon tea on a beautiful patio when I visited. Saw rare flowers I had never seen in my life!! Really worth the trek out + a nice detour on any roadtrip
title: A highlight of our trip! Really beautiful garden

body: Beautiful gardens, a map and plant guide would have been nice rather than just wandering aimlessly around. You can't get lost as all paths eventually go back to the bungalow. The collection of art, sculpture and furniture inside the bungalow was very interesting and you do get a guided tour of that.Entrance fee of Rs2,000 was a bit high especially as local people have to pay the same amount. A little effort in marketing the site better would attract more visitors without detracting from the tranquility of the gardens
title: An alternative to the beach

body: The place is nice and the bungalow is just a normal house with some paintings and pictures of the olden days.I feel 2k per person is too much for this.. the rates needs to be reasonable when there's a group of ppl, cz the tour is going to be only once for them and not done individually. Richmond Castle is way better.
title: Not worth the cost

body: Small garden walk, interesting design. The artwork within the house is diverse-paintings, sculptures. Unique pieces if you look closely. The road getting there was small-take a tuk or a high clearance vehicle .
title: A good day trip within Western Provence

body: The tuc-tuc ride to the gate is up some tiny little roads which is quite strange for such a notable attraction. The guided tour of the house was excellent with a very knowledgable guide who was able to describe a lot about Bevis Bawa and his life in Sri Lanka. It's great that he left his house and gardens to local people and they are doing a great job in presenting it to the public. The gardens are beautiful and this place is a lovely peaceful haven.
title: Lovely Gardens and House

body: Amazing gardens with plants and flowers to wander around. Guide was very informative regarding the history. House is full of objects and artwork collected over the years.
title: 1 of 4 Seniors in Sri Lanka

body: i have been before but went back for the second time,the story is very interesring ,and not a lot of people have herd about it,it is 2000 rupees to go in and a man to show you around.
title: worth seeing

body: As a traveller, we look for beauty everywhere - people, architecture, culture, trees and gardens. Sri Lanka scores very high in all categories. And when we found Bevis Bawa's garden called Brief (his father and brother, Geoffery were lawyers) and the documents they produced were "Briefs" Bevis was a writer, artist and gardener and his "Brief" is his garden. Every part of the garden is so cleverly designed, so deliberate, so carefully thought out; every view designed in such a way as to miss nothing. The magnificent grandeur of the trees - the choice of species, their placement in the landscape are exquistite. The scupture both beautiful and amusing. Don't miss it!
title: As a gardener I'm gobsmacked!

body: I am not clever enough to write a review for this property.I have been enjoying this since my childhood.
title: One and only

body: Brief & Lunuganga gardens are almost a competition between two brothers, with plenty of family money, to design & build their dream garden. The admission to Brief is 2,000 LKR which includes the house compared to 1,500 LKR for Lunuganga which is just a 1 hour garden tour. I liked the formal curved stairs to the main house & the sheltered courtyards with statues & wall hangings.The house at Brief is much better maintained than the main house at Lunuganga where I stayed 10 years ago & recently visited.Australian artist, Donald Friend, stayed at Brief and his legacy are several pottery faces and sketches.Both brothers were gay and their choice of art work reflects their tastes.Well worth a visit. But have your tuk tuk or car wait for you while you visit as it is out of the way.
title: Wonderful garden & access to house unlike Lunuganga

body: Totally enchanting location beautiful landscape and stunning variety of flowers trees and shrubs a must for garden lovers. I feel the cost of ticket justified would highly recommend. So much better than sitting on the beach ...
title: Magical

body: At 2000 rupees at the time of writing, its too expensive for what it offers. An aimless walk in a garden and a house. It’s quite difficult to get to as well. Rather spend the couple of hours at the lovely Bentota beach.
title: Too expensive

body: Its a lovely quiet spot away from roads and houses. We walked around the garden first exploring the different areas and interesting statues etc - best for me was the courtyard with amazing bat lilies I've never seen before.Each group has a personal tour of the house - luckily the tour ahead of us had started by the time we got there, so we able to relax and wait on the terrace. The house itself is interesting with pictures and photos, apparently now owned by old staff of Mr Bawa. As others have said it is quite expensive, and is cash only. There is nothing else around the area for drinks or snack so be prepared. Overall I preferred Lunuganga which isn't too far away but I guess that's a personal preference.
title: Interesting exploring the garden plus a tour of the house

body: “Brief Garden” is in Darga Town, Beruwala near Aluthgama about 45 km south from Colombo. Previously known as “Bawa’s Garden”, but now it is called “Brief Garden”. This is a private property owned by Mr. Bevis Bawa.He is the brother of the famous architect Mr. Geoffrey Bawa.Charming landscaped garden with sheltered paths with trees and various types of plants. The Bawa’s Bungalow is in the middle of the land with ancient furniture and pictures etc., But now the garden seems to be neglected and not maintained properly. The road to the garden is very narrow, a three-wheeler, motor cycle or a small car is recommended. If you go in a hired vehicle ask them to wait for you or return in one-hour time since there is no way to return back. The place seems to be needed lot of attention. I think it is better if they consider using it for tourism or even convert as a Boutique Hotel.
title: Wonderful Landscapping

body: We visited Brief Garden from Bentota Beach. It was a quick trip there (10 min) through the countryside. The roads are very narrow, so a tuktuk is recommended but a small car can make it too. Have your driver stay and wait for you, as there are no other drivers there and you’re in the middle of nowhere! The staff at the gardens were friendly and the gardens themselves were beautiful. It was like being transported back in time, we could imagine the dinner parties or daytime picnics to be had! Be warned there were a lot of mosquitoes, so spray yourself beforehand and it will be a more enjoyable walk! After exploring the gardens on our own, the staff on duty gave us a tour of the house, pointing out the unique artworks and people who were connected to the history of this place. We were given cold towels during our tour as well. The price is 2000 rupees per person (not 1000 rupees as I saw on several other postings) for the garden and house tour, but this is clearly posted at the entrance. Highly recommend for an hour of exploring and to get out of Bentota for a bit!
title: Intriguing Natural Escape

body: Bawa Garden or Brief garden is a picturesque landscaped garden that lies few kilometers inland of Bentota. With stone steps, shady paths, esthetically structured trees and plants, this is a splendid tranquil space to wander and explore. The garden and the colonial villa set in its middle was owned by Bewis Bawa, the brother of the famous architect Geoffrey Bawa.
title: Wonderful

body: 'Brief' is a gorgeous tropical garden with history, can also go into the original bungalow which has some artworks by Bawa's friends. I was surprised to see a big price increase - as was my tuk tuk driver who said it has doubled since last month. Price now 2000 LKR, which is a bit steep. Don't know if I would've gone at that price, still a lovely garden though.
title: Beautifully landscaped garden - and price hike

body: Our driver told us about this place as we had some knowledge of the Bawa family. It is a lovely garden and a unique house built to suit the conditions. The house contains some nice art and furniture and the current custodian provides a guided tour included in the ticket price
title: Resplendent Respite in tranquil setting

body: Went to the 9.30am viewing with a guide. 1500 lkr. Very lush and green with a large variety of plants and foliage. Beautiful views with water on 2 sides of the estate. Used to be a rubber plantation. Took about an hour to walk around. It is not a flower garden and cannot be compared to Butchart Gardens in Canada. About 20 acres.
title: Serene Gardens Well Maintained

body: A mixture of beautifully maintained gardens and the art of Australian Donald Friend makes this a fascinating discovery. The site was bequeathed to the head gardener on the death of Bevis Bawa, and he certainly has an intriguing tale to tell.
title: FASCINATING PROVENANCE

body: Visited the brief garden near bentoto Sri Lanka for the second timeA very special place beautifully keptEasy by tuktuk from town
title: Stunning garden

body: Do drive there with a car and driver. It is located in the countryside and not accessable by touring bus. Entry 5 euro per person. Truly stunning location that gives an impression how Sri Lankan nature was in the 20th century with peaceful villages and green mountains. If you wish to find some peacefulness you will enjoy the garden and surroundings with ricefields ao. This garden is more architectural than botanical. Educated guide tells about architect Major Bawa and his family history.
title: Singalese heritage garden

body: just a green lush garden. one has to pay 1500 lkr as a entrance fee & ring a bell , a person wil open the gate & wil show you the way to enter the garden in a narrow path. after you finish the garden you can climb to the apartment side .. a man vl come to take you around & tel you the history of that place & about the owner of the garden . you can skip, not much recommended
title: not much to see

body: Architecturally beautiful landscaped garden. Very clever layout with plenty of interest. If you are just looking for some pretty flowers then this is not the garden for you. If however you appreciate landscape design then you will be well rewarded. After visiting the garden, we then had a guided tour of the house, which in itself was fascinating. At LKR1000, this was very good value. We spent close on two hours here.
title: Fascinating garden and house

body: We had a guide on this day we didn’t even know he was taking us to this garden ,wow what a surprise ,we enjoyed it immensely .Garden was wonderful with all its different sections ,the house and artworks and Bevis Barwa stories ,all the goingson in his home ... AMUSING ... a must see !!!
title: Surprised

body: Nice maintained garden in near Bentota But entry fee is too much and also no one is there to guide in garden
title: Can be skipped if not interested in Architechture

body: Unlike Lunuganga, this attraction can be visited at any time. We hired a tuk-tuk from our hotel in Bentota for 150rupees and the driver waited for us-the visit lasted just over an hour but you can dawdle as much as you like. You really do get the impression of this being a 'secret' garden after the journey there-hidden behind a wall in the middle of densely wooded area yet close enough to Bentota. You can visit the house with its various artworks, along with a fascinating account of Bevis Bawa and his life among the top brass in spite of his sexual proclivities. A totally unusual experience and, if you visit early like us at 9.30am, you might get the place to yourselves!
title: Secret hideaway!

body: This place was a bit smaller than we expected. We came straight from visiting Lununganga and it just doesn’t compare. We spent about 30-45 minutes there and that included an explanation of sorts about some of the art work and the house. It is a nice garden but not maintained to the same standard as his brothers. We enjoyed it as we like gardens, but it was extremely hot with no offer of relief from that anywhere, there isn’t much to it and it just felt like something was missing somehow.
title: Small

body: This is nice museum where you can see the Bawa house, paintings, house items, life style of him, statues and etc. there is nice garden. those who like paintings and nature should visit this place.
title: Nice place to visit!

body: We did this as a day excursion from Colombo, and though our driver had a terrible time finding the place, eventually we made it (it doesn't help that when you get to the road that's actually marked "Brief Garden" you'll be met by a guard telling you it's under repair and you have to go a different way that's not marked. The tour starts in the gardens, where you're free to wander around, stopping at various pools and lookouts. At the house you may well be met by a guide--ours was the owner himself--and that's where the real fun begins. There are statues and paintings all over the place, some indeed mildly erotic, but many just plain fun. My favorite may have been the whole wall made out of wine bottles. There's something wonderful on every wall and around every corner. Even a polished coconut on a coffee table looks like a piece of art.
title: Come for the garden, stay for the art

body: If you have excess money and wasting time you can visit a place like this.I visited with my family this place. it is not as we expected .The service they offered is very poor.Nothing special in the garden. I do not recommend anyone to visit here as We visit all the garden leisurely in 15 minutes time. some areas are not maintaining as well.
title: The Worst Place I have ever visited .

body: A short drive from Bentota this is well worth taking the visit.It seems there is no need to book. We just showed up, were turned loose in the lush garden and then worked our way back to the old owners house for a guided tour.The property is not crowded, it is well maintained and quietly welcoming. Well worth the effort.
title: Absolutely wonderful.

body: Good place to visit .. cool place and more old items to see..garden is very beautiful one day is not enough to see all things ... i like to visit again
title: Excellent landscaping

body: Buried in the middle of the Srilankan countryside Brief Gardens is a wonderful peek back in time to when Bevis Bawa designed a garden full of indigenous trees & Shrubs.We saw too many species of birds to count, & were privileged to see an iguana & a mongoose.The house is fascinating look at the way this remarkable man lived.
title: Beautiful Gardens & House

body: The garden is about 10 kms from Bentota and is, for Sri Lanka, quote expensive to get in - 1,000 rupees. The garden is pleasant but not exceptional. The house is shabby and the artwork is drab and not very interesting. You are not given access to the upstairs. Personally, for anyone who has seen gardens or botanical gardens elsewhere or historical houses, this is not worth the visit and certainly not at that price. We had made a special stop off in Bentota for it but we were disappointed,
title: Somewhat faded in all aspects

body: Amazing small garden and interesting house. An oasis of calm in the bustle of the nearby cities. A few more labels on the plants would enhance the visit. The tour of the house is quite short, but interesting. Lovely to get away from the beach for an hour or two.
title: Peaceful

body: Not too far from Bentota it is a must to pay a visit to Brief Garden - Bevis Bawa. The garden was made after cutting the rubber trees. The garden is designed by a landscape architect and is beautifully located on a hill overlooking the valley.The villa is also worthwile visiting. It contains a lot of art and old Dutch wooden furniture.
title: Wonderful garden and villa - a must when visiting Bentota

body: The extensive garden and country home of (in)famous Sri Lankan landscape architect, Bevis Bawa. Part of the charm of the place is that our tour was conducted by Mr. da Silva who was Bevis's head gardener for many years and who inherited the estate and still lives there. The planning of the garden, the rather outrageous gay life-style of Bevis, and his eclectic collection of art and photos are all brought to life by Mr da Silva. Lovely tranquil setting. Easily combined with a visit to Lunuganga, garden and home to Bevis's brother, Geoffrey.
title: Most interesting

body: A former rubber estate, this garden was the creation of Bevis Bawa, brother of Geoffrey Bawa, well known Sri Lankan architect. Set in 5 acres it is a stunning wild, beautiful and slightly erotic garden. Set around a beautiful house. It is open all day, and a guide will take you around the public areas of the house, but you are free to walk the grounds. The estate was divided when Bevis died, with the great proportion of the estate being left to the workers, and the house and garden being left to an architectural practice.
title: More than Brief

body: You can appreciate the amazing effort that has been made over many years to get and keep this garden in such a wonderful state. It is peaceful walking around and appreciating the landscape architecture. The house is also worth visiting and the tour guide we had was most informative. Definitely worth the effort to get to and the LKR1000 admittance.
title: Beauty in the middle of nowhere

body: The minute I read about this place, I just knew I had to visit it. The grounds are simply gorgeous- a tamed tropical rustic maze of interconnecting paths and steps interlaced with stone ornaments and pools. The Japanese inspired terraced water feature is wonderfully serene.The villa, perched above the gardens is beautifully airy with lots of Bawa’s eclectic art collection and photographs on display. The guide is very knowledgeable and passionate about the Bevis Bawa story - well worth a visit.
title: Heavenly Hideaway

body: Third time to this querky and interesting place. I took my visitors who loved it. A fan of the Bawa brothers anyway. The guides are excellent. Highly recommended.
title: Return

body: Brief Gardens by Bevis Bawa - This was not on my itinerary, but found it in my tour book the night before. I asked my driver if we could visit the next am. Was so very pleased I did. Serene and peaceful place to enjoy wonderful gardens, secret green spots in the landscape. I thought it would be a great place for children, or adults, to play hide-and-go-seek! Birds and the peaceful breeze through the leaves and palms is the only sounds you hear. Painting, sculpture, ceramics and books dress the modest cottage. Wonderful place for a peaceful visit for a couple of hours....
title: a lovely place to get lost...

body: This is a good place to spend an hour to an hour and a half. The gardens aren't what the must have been when Bevis Bawa was alive but they're still spectacular. The house tour is interesting as well.
title: Interesting Venue

body: Fascinating place to visit if you are travelling to or from Bentota. I wasn't expecting to see something like this tucked away in the jungle and it was a lovely surprise to be able to wander around the gardens and the house. I would love to been able to see all the nooks and crannies in the house, but we were able to experience was really cool. Interesting mix of cultures and the past.
title: Beautiful garden with interesting history

body: Those who are interested in landscaping, Open space and Architecture should visit this place. The creator is a few decades ahead of his time.This place is not Wheel-chair accessible and they should think of some way to overcome the issue soon.The other big issue is that they have no Risk Assessment and Management Plan.Nice experience and one would not regret going.Cheers
title: " Brief " Encounter !

body: The garden, hidden away amongst the dense jungles of Sri Lanka, is well worth a stroll but it's the bungalow and it's history that will capture your interest. The colonial bungalow where Bevis Bawa lived and entertained his guests is a glimpse into the heady days and lifestyle of Sri Lanka's most famous landscaper and friend of the rich and famous including actors Peter Finch and Vivien Leigh who stayed at the bulgalow. .
title: The Garden is good but the history of the Bungalow is the main attraction

body: Otherwise skip, as the sight is quite remote from Bentota. This garden and the adjacent villa are Bewis Bawa's magnificent work. The sight is full of artsy and homoerotic artifacts, sculpture and furniture. The design is a blend of a modernist and Asian traditional styles. The house keeper profoundly explained to us about the concept and history of the house and its dweller. Nice place.
title: Worth for arts and architecture enthusiasts

body: Beautifully kept house and garden, owned by a gardener! A short tuk tuk from town thru windy narrow lane ways. Interesting history and artworks around the house.
title: Inspiring garden

body: Nice maintained garden in near bentonaBut entry fee is too much and also no one is there to guide in garden
title: Good maintained garden

body: I go here , 2 or 3 times a year. It never fails to inspire me. Not as well maintained as perhaps it could be but never the less the design works and has held up very well over the decades.Bevis Bawa certainly was a master of combining the best of Western approach making the most of Sri Lankan flora. It is a must visit for anyone with interest in gardens, architecture or art. A trained eye with understand this amazing place and the skill that went into creating it.Combine the day with his brother's, Geoffrey Bawa, home and garden not far away. Lunuganda . Such talented siblings.
title: Certainly still one of my favourite places to visit in Sri Lanka

body: Breathtakingly beautiful gardens where one can spend hours exploring. Quiet, peaceful, enchanting! Extremely well maintained. The house was very interesting with many paintings, interesting photographs of Bevis Bawa and captivating poetry. The caretaker was very nice and pointed out many things of interest. The owner, Mr Dooland de Silva was an excellent host and imparted an abundance of fascinating info about Bevis Bawa and the history of the garden.
title: Magnificent!!

body: This is the Garden and the House of Bewis Bawa, the brother of another famous architect Geoffrey Bawa. This has developed by Bewis Bawa from 1920s. The Garden with long walks under the shady tall trees and possible seating here and there, make you wander for hours.The house has its unique features, giving it a character.
title: Mesmerizing Garden and an Iconic house

body: This is the home and garden of Bevis Bawa, Aide-de-Camp to 2 British governors of Ceylon and elder brother of famed architect Geoffrey. Visited this place as a result of being turned away from Geoffrey Bawas 'Lunuganga' because we were 10 minutes late! Talk about bureaucracy gone mad. Those of you who have travelled to Sri Lanka and other Asian countries know that travel times can vary dramatically, apparently this fact eludes the managing trust of Lunuganga.Anyway, Brief Garden is a delightful surprise, meandering garden paths that can end suddenly and others that take you to amazing surprises. Your ticket gives you access to the gardens and house (unlike Lunuganga) and a very informative guide that worked for Bevis himself. He has a wealth of information on the gardens, house and the man himself. Ask him about the famous visitors to the property like Sir Lawerence Olivier, Vivien Leigh and Australian artist Donald Friend who came for a weekend and stayed for 6 years!Do yourselves a favour and when in Bentota visit 'Brief' Garden. You will be enchanted.
title: Artists Jungle Retreat

body: We thoroughly enjoyed visiting these charming gardens. We thought it was nice that we could just wander around on our own without having to go on a guided tour. At the end of our walk the caretaker showed us round the house which was also very interesting. Bevis Bawa seemed to be an amazing man! Definitely well worth a visit!
title: A beautiful area.

body: Amazing experience and such beautiful place with some exceptional gardening.. and must mention the owner who is so knowledgeable and have worked with Mr. Bawa himself for so long is an amazing person. The gardens are from around the world just mention the French, English, American and the Japanese. the diversity of the plants, trees are also a marvel. a ticket is only priced at 1000 LKR and if you wish to dine there they also arrange lovely romantic meal, go an experience the life of Bevis Bawa and his miracle of work..
title: Bevis Bawa's Brief Garden..

body: Grab a tuk tuk to Brief garden, if going by car you will struggle with some of the paths as when approaching this area the roads become narrow and thin (ideal for a tuk tuk). There are sign post guiding you to brief garden. A small fee just under 500 rupees (£2.50p) per person for an entry cost of visiting the house within brief garden. I would advise to wear mosquito spray although we never encountered any at the time we went they are there frequently but been told they are jungle mosquitos. Brief garden is runned by a lovely family and are dedicated to provide information about the paintings/photos/ landscape and sculptures here. Max time you would need is only a hour, the garden isn't huge but quite peacefull walking around with my partner.
title: Easy Excursion

body: Its an amazing experience which we had on 29th april 2018. Little bit of isolated location. Not much of popularity with the locals. Access to the location is lityle bit difficult if you are travelling by public transport. You have to take tuk tuk form aluthgama, cost LKR 400. It has its uniqueness but entrance frees are little bit high for the locals even. The ticket price display board make miss-understand for foreigners, 300LKR only to visit garden. 1000LKR for both garden and House. house contents collection of Bevis Bava and some of his friends. However when we looked at the paintings and monuments, we can identify that Bevis prefer to stay alone from the society and he enjoyed his homosexual lifestyle with the locals.
title: Lost in a Wonderland

body: This is a beautiful place but garden is not maintained properly. No cafeteria. Not worth for money. It would be a great place of attraction if managed in good manner.
title: Beautiful architecture

body: The Bevis Bawa Brief Garden, the managed home of a wealthy eccentric old Brit, he lived an alternative lifestyle here, perhaps the less said about that the better, but his home and garden are simply beautiful. A small but incredibly peaceful location, one wonders how these locations come to be or how the wealthy land owners settle on the place. You cannot help but think about life in Sri Lanka back in the early 20th century or beforehand at the height of colonialism and desire for such hedonistic tropical retreats. Here was a man who received visitors such as Edward VIII at his well attended private parties…
title: Beautiful garden, peaceful location, odd man...

body: Yes, imagine yourself in the house of an Edwardian gentleman somewhere in SE England... and yet the plants are too exotic, the temperature too hot and the humidity too high!This is the house and garden of Bevis Bawa, brother of the famous architect, Geoffrey.It is difficult to find: our very experienced driver-guide has been here many times before but he had to ask local people the way on several occasions. There are no signs pointing to the place!Once parked, ring the doorbell. Once you have paid the 1000 LKR each, you will be a instructed to explore the garden by yourself and then make your way in to the house.The gardenis absorbing with its many paths, wonderful flora and nooks.There are plenty of photo opportunities outside and in.Once you are inside the house, you will be met and given an on-and-off tour of the rooms. Interesting furniture and fascinating photos.There is no cafe or shop here! Thank goodness!Would I return? Yes!
title: A world away... imagine yourself in a different time...

body: Stepping into the Brief reminded me of one of my childhood favorites: "The Secret Garden". Its eclectic landscaping - fusing manicured lawns with patches of wild herbage -makes this a unique garden. Although this is not a large place, there is a lot of detail to absorb and we spent more than two hours in the garden discovering various statues and artifacts that illuminated several aspects of Bevis Bawa's life. Brief is an amazing place to relax and contemplate nature.
title: Enchanting, serene, quaint oasis

body: The garden is very quaint and one can only imagine what it must have been like in its day. The collection of artwork and history is interesting too. If you have time and are interested in gardens and art then definitely pop through.
title: Lovely spot if you have time on your hands

body: It's not much big garden .but inside small area there are some special things to see about architecture. Because owner of garden was very famous architecture in Sri Lanka.you have to buy a ticket for enter.
title: Garden park

body: Its most exciting short trail to the house. Please do go the full circle which leads to the house. Unique plants and flowers can be seen. The house itself has artifacts and old photographs which will tell the story. Be mindful to apply mosquito repellent as its a walk in the jungle in the middle of nowhere. Its simply beautiful & calming. Do pay attention to what the guide says, he is from the household and does have some interesting stories about Bevis Bawa himself.
title: Must see place for landscape/ architecture

body: A little bit off the beaten track, but well worth it. The large garden is so cleverly designed with many levels and features, it's a peaceful space. The house is beautifully designed too, with many interesting photos and memorrabilia. The huge painting on the wall by Donald Friend tells the story of the area, and there are many other lovely pieces. Small groups only.
title: Beautiful Space

body: At both sides of the entrance lane two beautiful sculptures on pillars to lure one in to visit this garden.And we were not disappointed, there was throughout plenty to discover, flowering trees and plants, narrow lanes, lined with old tree roots like sculptures, leading to small sitting and wide viewing area's. Intriguing sculptures. The house breathes history with its old photographs, artefacts and paintings. Especially the very large mural depicting Sri Lanka, in all its small details. The house, as well as the garden, is the perfect setting in its lush and tropical green landscape. Not to be missed while in Sri Lanka!
title: Intriguing and enchanting!

body: A wonderful visit to a serene beautiful garden and house. The staff were lovely and we learned a lot. It's a little of the beaten track so take a tuk-tuk.
title: Lovely quiet place

body: Certainly is well hidden and not very easy to find but very well kept and lovely setting. Entrance fee a little steep for what there is to see but I imagine the up keep is a huge job. Very well maintained garden with lots of places to hide and escape. A few statues and ornaments to look at and some beautiful flowers. A couple of water features, not he worlds largest house and garden but nice to escape and take in the peace and quiet. House is ok but a very small tour. Can tick it off my list of tourist attractions.
title: A hidden garden

body: It was a longer Tuk Tuk ride than we'd anticipated, but none the worst for that. Both house and gardens are well worth the effort. We weren't racing on to another destination so we whiled away a couple of hours wandering around the gardens. The staff kindly allowed me to borrow a chair for sketching.
title: Wonderfully serene visit

body: We quite enjoyed our visit here - there isn't a huge amount to see .It cost 1000LKR. A tea room would be a bonus. We were taken there by our Tuk tuk driver from Suranga Tours - who i cant recommend enough. We much preferred Lunuganga gardens.
title: Short visit

body: We felt this was a waste of time. Not much to see either in the garden or house. 500 rupees would have been better value. Very unwelcoming. No cafe or drinks, unlike guidebook. Would advise against visiting unless desperate for something to do!
title: Emperor's new clothes

body: This is an amazing garden in Sri Lanka and one of a beautiful garden we have visited. It hard to find but once you enter this magical garden, you'll forget everything. We walk around and enjoyed the beauty of the nature and emerald garden decors. Perfect location to capture some unique photos of plants and birds. The house is also ok but not much to visit inside. The staff member who issued tickets, simply NOT POLITE and can't smile even. But later he explain us about the photos and some places in the house. Except the impolite staff member, others are really good. It was a totally different experience and worth to visit!!
title: Hidden gem in Sri Lanka

body: We enjoyed visiting this beautiful property together with the history of this Aristocrratic Family in the Times of the British colony. A great artist and architect of gardens design. Definitely recommendable. Pity that the foundations of Sri Lanka do not invest to keep it nicer. Renovations works are needed because it is falling a liitle bit apart in the gardens.
title: Great place

body: This was a really cool thing to do. The Tuk Tuk ride is fun, it takes you off the beaten track into the jungle. Upon arrival you ring on a big gong bell. A man lets you in on the side gate and allows you to walk around the gardens yourself and when you are ready to enter the house. You can see it was probably once a beautiful garden but don't expect the botanical gardens with gorgeous flowers and lush grass. It is more rustic. Upon entering the house, it reeks up hedonistic decadent parties once upon a time. It is a great house for entertaining. Bevis apparently loved to party. The art and antiques are beautiful. It is worth the trip. Something different - hard to explain.
title: off the beaten track

body: Loved strolling around the gardens and through the house. Fascinating to see how it has been maintained and to reflect on that era, good and not so good. Appreciated the gay art.
title: Amazing gardens, place has a quaint old world queer feel - hope those boys did well from the estate

body: did not know much about this place ,but three people in one day recommended,and was very pleased to have gone.look it up first to see if its what you like.
title: what an interesting place to visit

body: This was one of the highlights of our time in Sri Lanka. If you enjoy gardens, art and architecture you should not miss this. Brief is hidden away inland of busy Bentota and is a tranquil oasis created by Bevis Bawa, brother of well known architect, Geoffrey Bawa. Previously a rubber plantation, the gardens have been beautifully designed and the house is full of beautiful art works by Bawa and his friends, including Donald Friend from Australia. You need to ring the bell when you arrive and time your visit so that you can then go to Geoffrey Bawa's country house at Lunuganga which is also well worth a visit.
title: Fascinating garden and house

body: This place take a long time to get to, but takes about 30 mins to visit. Odd combination of manicured gardens, eclectic sculptures, paintings and house. Journey to and from gives an interesting insight into rural Sri Lankan subsistence living.Perfect example of English eccentricity.
title: Odd place and not a lot to see

body: The Brief Garden is a must to visit. It is tranquil and yet totally alive with bird song. At the villa we were met by a guide who informed us about the history of the house and garden. The gardens are beautiful however, we would have lingered longer in the garden if there had been a tea room or refreshments to buy then we could have just sat and taken in the full experience.
title: Tranquil Garden

body: What a hidden gem! One of the most impressive, calm and beautiful places we have visited. We visited as a family with adult children. Walked around the garden - perfect for pictures. We also saw some monkeys! Off the beaten path, especially from Kalutara, but we had a driver with us who knew the way. Fascinating scenery and a must stop if you are in Bentota.Guide was very polite and informative. Only suggestion is to consider opening a gift shop. Lots of potential to sell tasteful postcards of garden views or reproductions from some of the art in the house.
title: An absolute gem

body: You have travel deep into the village to find this place. So if you are going with your own vehicle then make sure about route. However it is a hidden gem. Beautiful landscaping with proper maintenance. You have to get a ticket at the entrance.
title: Beautiful Landscaping...

body: A visit to the Brief Garden and bungalow is a must if you are in the Aluthgama area. Fascinating history, imaginative landscaping, lovely building, I could have moved in immediately!
title: Amazing!

body: The gardens and house are really lovely. You're free to explore the large garden then a guide will take you around the house. The gardens are filled with sections of tropical plants and features which are truly peaceful. The house sits at the top of a hill with calming views and is filled with personal objects and photos of interest depicting Bevis Bawa's relationships with many famous individuals such as Prince Edward (later Edward VIII) Lawrence Olivier and Agatha Christie. The house and garden contain interesting pieces of art as well as phalic statues. Those with with a less open mind or narrow thinking of the world may wish to avoid
title: An amazing and eclectic house and garden

body: We felt this was well worth visiting and the entrance fee of 1000 LKR per person was reasonable. Very peaceful gardens that you can wander through and explore at your own pace. After visiting the gardens a friendly guide showed us the house and explained the history. Having read some other reviews on TripAdvisor I would suggest that if you are homophobic then don't visit - if you aren't, then enjoy the beauty and serenity of the garden and finding out about the interesting history of the house and the Bawa brothers.
title: Beautiful gardens, really interesting history

body: We were left to wander around the gardens to try and work out where to go. There are some nice areas even if overgrown which almost adds a sense of discovery. However the naked statues littered around don't prepare you for the house which has art workd and even a poem talking about how Bevis liked young boys. This overshadows the whole trip.
title: Ornate gardens but has an open history of paedophilia

body: A lovely walk through the grounds around the winding paths was had, followed by a walk around the house which had some querky items like the outdoor bath and statue ( see if you can find it) ideally take mosque spray with you as we got a number of bites whilst in the gardens.
title: Loverly walk

body: We spent about an hour or so here. It was nice, but the weather was really humid that day and our kids were getting a bit cranky. The gardens are well kept and we would love to live in this house, it's lovely. It's 1000 rupees per adult but overall I thought it was worth it
title: Really nice place

body: Already the way to brief garden is a little adventure and makes lot of fun. You pass little village(s), get the feeling driving though jungle.Brief garden itself is an oasis of silence. It is designed/arranged very well with nice trees, flowers, tiny lakes. The house itself a gem, with artistic paintings, a wonderful view. Interior is arranged very well.First we were skeptic about the idea going there but it is more than worth.
title: it is worth a visit - hidden secret

body: A true jungle in a village. Calm and quiet place, very cool in every climate and easy access from Mathgama Town. Environmental friendly location visited by many foreign guests. The site is well looked after by the people in charge. A must for any one who is interested in Eco-friendly location.
title: Major Bevis Bava Brief

body: On arrival my husband and I were left to explore the grounds on our own and we could take as much or little time to do this. Warning - Don't forget to apply insect repellent before visiting unlike us - The mosquitos enjoyed feasting on our flesh !! As we arrived at the house we were joined by our guide who was eloquent in describing how and why Bevis created the house and grounds the way he did. The guide was clearly a great admirer of the great man. A lovely way to spend the afternoon.
title: lovely and peaceful

body: Bevis Bawa was arguably the more talented of the two brothers as far as landscaping is concerned. However, it is somewhat sad to see the whole establishment slowly but surely falling in maintenance standards - it requires more than gate collections to maintain the gardens and establishment of this magnitude.. This time around it was also somewhat disturbing to see the evidence of the obvious debauchery that took place at The Brief during the man's life. But then, who is to stand in moral judgement over these matters...
title: Marginal decline from the earlier visit

body: history teaches us that Lunuganga is a haven for visitors, but I was proved wrong when I visited the Brief Garden after many years to meet with its current owner, Dooland De Silva. he was friendly, quick to realize that we have met earlier (despite the hundreds who walk in). Bevis Bava was an unsung hero, really was the pioneer behind brilliant landscaping back in the days, much before his younger, famous brother started his own project to outdo his elder brother. Brief has character and the people who run it make it even better. it is important that your host makes you feel special and the stories of Bevis is humorous and funny. Donald Friend's works are apparent at the Brief Garden, the journey is more than memorable. recommend this 1,000% over anything. a must to be visited by all means
title: The Brief Garden - It is surreal

body: I'd read about this place before coming to Sri Lanka and as I was staying nearby I thought I'd give it a go. A couple of friends I met on my holiday joined me (we visited Richmond Castle on the same day) and we all really enjoyed it.It's worth being aware that it is quite remote and a little difficult to get to, and is not like an immaculately maintained National Trust stately home or perfectly manicured public garden. It was once someone's home and has been kept that way. It feels natural and atmospheric and we really liked that about it, as it was less touristy and therefore more relaxing. Your enjoyment of the brief garden will, as with most things in life, be based on your own personal taste but don't let that put you off visiting!
title: Hard to find but enjoyable

body: The Brief garden is about a 30 minute tuk tuk ride away from Bentota (we paid 300 rupees for 2 of us including driver waiting time). Entrance to the garden is 1000 rupees each. The ride was so picturesque through real Sri Lankan lush country. The garden has got a nice history but as keen garden lovers and members of National Trust, visiting this garden was disappointing and overpriced. The garden was owned by Bevis Bawa who was a self taught artist and sculpture. He was also a Sri Lankan actor and there are photos of him with Vivienne Leigh and other actors. He was a heavy smoker, drinker, and homosexual which is reflected in the paintings and many sculptures in the garden and house. The garden is not very big and it took about an hour and a half to walk around the garden and visit the house with the guided tour. It was landscaped by his brother Geoffrey, whose own garden Lunuganga is supposed to be a lot better to visit but we didn't get the time. It's a pleasant enough walk around the garden but nothing really that impressive, but we saw some lovely sunbirds and even a snake! A lot of the paths needed cleaning. There are interesting items of art and furniture around the house but sadly it didn't live up to our expectations, nor to what we had heard. Some sculptures seemed in need of a good clean from the overgrowth. Definitely not worth the entrance fee, but a lovely ride.
title: Nice ride,disappointing and over priced garden!

body: The worst place I have ever been. As I remember entrance fee is around Rs.300 just to see the garden. 1000 for house plus the garden (per person) utter waste of money. Dry untidy place. 😑 Literally nothing to see.In need of a serious maintenance and entrance fee reconsideration.
title: Disappointed

body: Brief Garden is somewhat off the radar as a regular tourist destination in Sri Lanka is concerned but well worth a visit if you are in Bentota. The garden itself is located down a narrow lane way and would not be accessible by any vehicle larger than a mini van. Entrance fee is a little steep at 10,000 rupees but if it's going towards the garden upkeep then so be it. The garden has some beautiful landscaping features including a Japanese garden, numerous water features, stone stepped terraces, brick archways and the original residence which houses many artefacts and paintings owned by the Bevis Bewa family.
title: Lovely Place

body: First of all, don't forget that this was Bevis's private house so don't expect to find a palace or a museum when you come here because you won't find that. The place is very remote and difficult to access, which in my opinion makes the whole experience more charming but some may not enjoy this.The garden is big and well looked after, and if you spend enough time walking around it you may see some cute animals. Make sure you sit down and enjoy the clean air and sounds of nature for a while if you go.The house is nice too, but I'm sure it has many interesting features that I missed (as I am not an architect and I'm not familiar with many building techniques) I think it would be really nice if the staff provided some kind of information about who Bevis was and why this place is so amazing (perhaps a guided tour every 30 min?)I would recommend to visit this place if you're not travelling from too far, but maybe it's not worth spending 2-3 hours driving just for that.
title: Beautiful garden and nice house

body: Garden was nice and fairly maintained, but the guide wasnt friendly enough. Hoped to see something more than this....
title: The visit doesn't worth the money u pay....

body: ... combined with a unique garden experience, some kind of jungle, art objects, seldom flowers, the extraordinary bat-headed lily just finished to bloom and (never seen before) porcelaine roses now in it's best red colour, all incredible, sunk deep into the soul and heart. A must for people who seek silence and beauty.
title: A part of touchable personal history ...

body: Brief Garden offered an opportunity for us to get away from the beach resort for a while. The garden itself is hidden away, but well worth the effort involved in finding it. Beautiful tropical plants at every turn and an interesting house filled with art that gives a insight in to the life of the owner - Bevis Bawa. Hidden Gem!
title: Beautiful Gardens - another Hidden Gem

body: We came here on our penultimate day. It's a bit tricky to find but a bit of research and a local driver is a great help and worth the trip.It's like walking into one of the exotic plant houses at Kew. I noted 5 species of Strelitzia (bird of Paradise flower) within minutes of arriving and the scarce bat lily was flowering when we visited. The garden slopes and is severally terraced with a central mini-cascade and a beautiful mini walkway lined with ginger plants. We spotted a humming bird but which flew off before it could be identified. One of the Banyan Trees was also flowering and I think that the Lord Buddha was born beneath one so they are revered for religious reasons.The guide in charge also showed us the house ground floor with some of Bevis Bawa's works of art. A remarkable character over 6 and a half feet tall during his adult life and with a certain Bohemian taste in art. We were delighted that we went.
title: Come to see a fine plant collection in a lovely setting

body: It is not easy to find it, but local taxi/rickshaw drivers know it well and google maps also can help. It is a true garden architect and artistic place, giving a special feeling of the decadent lifestyle by former owner. Really worth the effort!
title: Hidden gem!

body: One of best places I have visited in Down South. Very interesting and quite unexpected landscapes and architecture. Good for a leisurely walk among bizarre sculptures. Relaxing environment. A must visit.
title: Must Visit

body: Really enjoyed our visit here. It was definitely off the beaten track and our driver had never even heard of it but it was well worth going. Beautiful gardens and architecture. Highly recommended.
title: Beautiful gardens created by very interesting man

body: Beautiful and peaceful place to visit. It worth to see it. Would love to spent the twenties there...
title: Brief garden

body: Its not a proper garden like what we typically expect but everything is very natural and very soothing to your eyes.You can take a long walk through the garden and visit Bevis Bawa's banglow in the middle of the garden.
title: A relaxing few hours

body: Interesting private garden and house to see even though it has the regular plants as everywhere in the region. Some guidance is being offered in the house at the end of the whole tour. Not sure if 1000 rs. are an appropriate entrance fee but it was a nice short trip from Bentota (about 20min drive with rikshaw). Make sure your rickshaw driver waits for you..
title: Nice alternative program for approx. 2hrs

body: Visited here one afternoon in January for a half day trip from Bentota.A delight for both the gardener and anyone into house/style.I suggest a " Google" first or Wikipedia to read the background.Was able to take some excellent photographs.
title: An excellent 1/2 day visit

body: Got to know from #yamu.tv. We thought we were totally lost looking at the narrow road. Never thought that there would be vehicles. But there were some foreigners as well as locals. Entrance fee is 1000 rs per person to visit both garden and bungalow. Garden was breathtaking and we were so surprised with the architectural mind of Bewis bawa. We took some ideas from him to build our garden. Weather was soo cool and we felt amazing. The outside washroom and the bath area was amazing. It should be maintained than it's now. Better if the management can make the showers bath tubs and ponds working at least a bit. Nice place to hangout with families. Totally recommend it.
title: Beautiful garden

body: I have nothing to add to comments and pictures of earlier visitors. An adorable place, away from mass tourism. I would stay there forever...
title: Peaceful paradise garden and house

body: It worth to have a walk in this garden. We went with tuk tuk and have a short walk in the garden with guide who talked about the life of the owners. It was very interesting.
title: Good trip

body: The road to this place is really challenging - and it will make you wonder where on earth are you - but once you reach the place; every bump on the way is well worth it. It charges 3000 LKR for entry. The gardens are beautiful. The house tour will take you to days of glory of the european influence - its a must visit. I would love to visit again.
title: A surprise

body: Interesting jungle garden which is very peaceful and not busy. You can walk around the garden and then the house which has works of art created by Bevis Bawa . Saw a large monkey in the trees and also a minitor lizard. Take a picnic and enjoy the experience.
title: Peace in the jungle

body: 20 minutes from aluthgama passing paddy files and marshy land with lots of birds live and buffaloes grazing in the area. the garden a lone is a place you must visit.
title: a way out place to visit

body: Take a tuk tuk ride to the Bawa house and garden. Although garden needs some maintenance it's a lovely retreat with pathways through the tropical gardens. Aspects of the house are interesting as is the story of the talented Bawa brothers.
title: Interesting Story

body: I love the Bawa family history and went there as a kind of trip to the intimacy of Bewis. In fact, this is what you get... a good insight to yesteryear artistic life. Quite a good collection of artistic objects that remind you of Jean Cocteau.The garden is less enchanting except for the cascade and the century-old frangipan tree. I found the entry price of 1000 LKR too expensive, especially when there is no special fee for children under 18. Maybe, the fact that I am a regular visitor to the island makes me a bit more sensitive to this detail??!!!
title: A must-go place but a bit too pricey !

body: A wonderful garden built by Captain Bawa and it is well kept until now. Nice old photos remind the old days of Sri Lanka (Ceylon).
title: A mountain side feeling near to beach area

body: As a fan of Bawa's work, it was disappointing that our entrance to the property began with a bad start, firstly because the caretaker was not happy with our arrival at 2:30pm. Then sadly a member of our party was falsely accused of potential wrong-doing (I.e walking into an entry and bending to look at a painting whilst we used an outside restroom) -this was made by a female who lived on the property, not the caretaker. The caretaker' excuse for the yelling was thinly veiled by an explanation of previous trouble they had experienced with past visitors. The visit had now kicked off to a bad start and the caretaker did not offer to take us around the gardens and describe the beauty and landscape architecture. We were left to wander aimlessly through the overgrown gardens before having a tour of the house. It is clear that the caretaker is very knowledgeable, and he provided curt and limited explanations of the beautiful works inside the home itself.This was not what we expected especially with our comparison visit to Lunuganga, and some previous internet reviews prior to our visit to Brief Gardens. So you may need to piece together your own reading and research prior to visiting this tranquil acreage. It is clearly a magnificent property with alarmingly priceless artworks out in open display and unprotected from the elements. The property is in a hidden location along an unkept road that all but disappears at the gate. This journey itself is an adventure! The road is only just big enough for a 10 seater van. So sadly, our 1000 rupee entry fee pp was seen as very expensive for our party of 5, and it is a quandary because the property needs the funds from entry fees to maintain the property. Perhaps some better management and direction is required to preserve such a beautiful history.
title: Sad to see the Bawa name tarnished

body: A very enjoyable hour exploring this lovely japanese inspired garden. Touring the house afterwards was interesting and the guide was knowledgable and passionate about the home.
title: Beautiful gardens and gracious house guide

body: It is nice well kept and preserved garden for those who love nature...Natural is the word for this garden.
title: Well kept

body: The late Bevis Bawa created a botanical garden on his own private plot. And woaw, what a nice and cosy place it is. Now it is the trusted caretaker of the house who still maintains the magic, with its cherished botanical species. I sat with him and my then still very young daughter on the verandah, sipping a cup of tea. And it was an unforgettable experience. the luxury of a simple but tranquil haven. Good to forget the stress from home!
title: A must for those who love a splendid garden. Bevis was the brother of renowned architect Geoffrey Bawa

body: A majestic garden with loverly landscaping with a collection of interesting flora and fauna. The down side was the ridiculously high ticket prices. Just to see the place and have a walk through you have to spend rs. 300 per person. However there is no apparent time limit unless for the closing time. To see the bungalow it is 700. If they reduce the ticket prices and had opened a small restaurant/gift shop inside they could have earned more I guess.Sone parts of the garden are poorly maintained. Not doing justice for tue ticket prices at all. Go if you wanna grab some cool pics and feel the breeze.
title: Nice place to relax, but

body: Place is good, but SORRY to say it is not worth for 1000/=.. Maximum 15 min enough to walk around and see the house. I am feeling disappointed not about the money but about the time to travel (time wasted) to see just a house with garden.

You could glimps the beauty that was once there when the gardens were maintained but they have been taken over by weed. The house although interesting was very dark which made it impossible to really see the art work. Most of the art work was of naked men in various poses although there was one of Sri Lanka with prominent sights depicted as one large Mural. I don't think it was worth the hefty entry price.

body: We spent some strange time in the garden and were surprised not to see anything interesting. Were surprise d to lots of Homosexual paintings and sculptures. The garden and house are a little bit old fashioned and outdated. If you have a spare 1000 and you saw everything on the island than you are welcome.

body: Our driver recommended this garden & house and we were not disappointed. The gardens, started in 1928, have a huge variety of tropical plants and trees. They are presented in formal & non-formal settings and provide a beautiful walk, shaded by these huge natural structures. It's not an immaculately kept stately home in Britain, this is Sri Lanka and not enough gardeners to keep up, but that is part of the charm of this place. The house and it's history are fascinating and has been visited by many famous people including Edward VII, Vivienne Lee and the Danish Queen Mother. We were treated to a lovely cup of local tea in the garden by the house. We were the only visitors at the time and enjoyed the tranquility of this hidden gem.
title: Tropical Not a British Stately Home, but that is the charm.

body: Really enjoyed this experience, the artwork, library and sculptures were interesting. The garden was lovely and peaceful. Looking back I wish we had spent more time exploring both the house and gardens.
title: Lovely peaceful garden and home

body: a long ride. expected much..maybe that was the problem. i liked the location and the spread of the land..a large place with a fine vantage view, well utilised to build the bungalow there. the house itself is very spacious. stark and spartan though.

There are lots of interesting elements to the grounds and gardens, but they are very overgrown and very much in need of some maintenance to really bring out their beauty. The house is also quite nice with some beautiful modernist elements. I think it's worth a visit if you are in the area, but not really worth a special trip.

body: I decided to take a little excursion on my own, and the Brief Gardens was recommended by the hotel. So off I went with a personal driver. Once at the Gardens you will get a personal escort to take you around. I didn't know much about the garden itself ... apparently it was designed by a famous Sri Lankan architect. Apparently if you go in the morning opportunities to see birds and other wildlife would be a better bet. I enjoyed the few hours excursion.

body: It is a trip into the wild, with lovely views in every corner. Worth a visit for the price, and the way from bentota to the brief garden by tuk tuk is simply great!
title: Amazing nature all around

body: I have been to there for the first time some 10 years ago and ever since I have never found anything or anywhere, even to come closure to this place! It has not been changed and still carries the same attractiveness, it's own attractiveness! The unmatchable attractiveness!!! It is the playground of its creater! Yet it is the natural garden!
