body: Visited this preserved house and garden today, recommended by my tour guide. The walk around the garden leading to the house, was amazing. The layout and design of the portion of the house open to the public was most interesting, achieving comfort, many places to rest and enjoy the SriLamkan weather, and muse, yes of windows and busy areas to cool and filll with light. Recommended, historic, nice old photos.
title: Fabulous study on living space, abc character.

body: Although this is not popular among locals, it is one of best gardens I have seen with a unique connection to the surrounding and a mixture of several cultures. Try to visit there early after 8 a.m. as the number of visitors will be less during that time and also the birds chirping and fresh air around would be a place to meditate! They charge LKR 300 just to visit the garden but it is well worth the price and no time limit to stay inside. All you have to do is ring the bell once you arrive and when you leave. It is about 20 min tuk ride from Bentota railway and we managed to bargain the fair down to LKR 400 from LKR 700 (sometimes it is even LKR 1000)!! Be informed about the route to get there and also transport modes available with their fee. If you are travelling from Bentota you have to get to Aluthgama town and then go in Aluthgama-Mathugama road. Even the google maps are so accurate. Once you get closer, it is quite very rural area with less population and would need to keep the tuk for the returning journey as otherwise you have to walk about 2km to catch a bus to Aluthgama. But if you are truly a soulful traveler, I recommend you to walk that 2km through the shortcut and catch a bus which will give you a true essence of rural life. Even the buses are there once in every 30 min so if you are tight on schedule, you can always ask for the help of a lorry passing by and the people are so nice to give you free rides! (there are so many lorry based transportation). You can even have the information from the owners there at the garden. And don't forget to explore each and every corner of the garden!
title: Calm and soulful!

body: Very nice and beautiful garden and architecturally designed. Specially valuable for environmental lovers and people who are in to architectural studies.
title: Excellent artitectural version.

body: Bevis Bawa was clearly a talented man, and self-taught, unlike his UK-educated brother, who is probably more famous both locally and internationally. However, one gets the sense that it was Bevis who probably lived life to the fullest on his own terms (which may or may not be acceptable to all, but more later). The property is a bit out of the way, and not all locals seem to know the place as a lot of Web-sites suggest. Also, some of the access roads are not always operational due to roadwork, so it would be helpful to know beforehand the best path. Perhaps the tuk-tuks from Beruwala/Bentota are the best option. If not, GPS is surprisingly accurate, but for the roadwork. In a sign of his wry sense of humor, Bawa named this place Brief as his father got ownership/possession after winning a legal brief. Ring the bell to pay the entry fee, and then you are let into the garden for a self-guided tour. Props to earlier reviewers who suggested covered limbs to guard against aggressive fauna and flora (muchas gracias!). Once you finish the garden self-tour, go on up to the house and the caretaker, who was with Bawa during his twilight years of glaucoma, will give you a guided tour of the premises. He is extremely knowledgeable given his close personal association with the man and the property. He is patient and polite (although not overly affable, but don't let that fool you), as he waits for you to take pictures to heart's content, pointing out special spots along the way. One also gets the sense that he has experienced a fair share of hardships in his time, and one can't help but empathize. Former visitors/tenants of note at Brief include Laurence Olivier (pictures attest to this!). Now the potential concerns for some visitors: there are a lot of open phallic symbols, but that's perhaps acceptable as art, especially given the context of Bawa's relatively non-closeted lifestyle and orientation. What was a bit shocking though, was the fairly open display of trysts with local young boys, as evidenced by a sketch of one stanza of the poem, The Bawa of Brief, and other more subtle hints/signs along the way. LKR 1,000 entry fee, but worthwhile. Unfortunately, we were not offered tea/cookies, but that was not really a big deal!
title: Work of a Talented Man, but Disconcertingly Open Signs of Decadence

body: Lush, wonderful tropical garden designed by Bevis Bawa. Unfortunally, he got under marvelous shadow of his older brother Geoffrey Bawa. Love the artworks, some furniture designs and the weird statues in his garden. It works a long way to go from Negombo. Must see if you are around Bentota and Galle.
title: What a wonderful tropical garden!

body: The road up to Brief gardens is narrow and winding so don't go in a minivan. It was definately a hideaway for old Bevis and his young men, and it's a fab spot. There are lots of secret seating areas and amazing views. Watch out for the leeches, they'll get you if you wear open-toed sandals, but are easy enough to get rid of (google!)
title: Tropical Garden

body: First of all it's just place where original person lived. He had got interesting garden and house. Now it seams that not too much is invested to maintaine the garden. At the same time entrance fee is pretty expensive. It's also not so easy to get here. For our children it was boring and to hot to walk through the garden
title: Not the must

body: Whilst not the main event (apparently that is Lungana) this is a lovely find (although it is very hard to find) and a lovely example of tropical living in a bygone era. I arrived late in the day, had I planned better I'd have seen both and booked the lunch, but Brief (and you learn why it's called that), brief as it was, was a delight.
title: Lovely find

body: although not at the same level of the Luluganga estate this is quite a find, lovely details and momentos from the friends and visitors of the Bawa brothers
title: a lovely estate

body: We went to visit the place on the basis of earlier reviews. The Gardens were nice but the entry cost is prohibitive and definately not worth the effort.
title: Overhyped Place

body: Beautiful gardens, great day spent there and a very interesting guide who told us all about the house and about Bevis Bawa (including some... interesting details!)
title: Stunning gardens

body: Visited this place.Please check through Google maps and go. Easier than locals advise. They changed 300 to visit the garden which was pretty average.1000 lkr to peep through the house. Which was pointless for us.Any way it's a private place and somebody is selling bava's name to earn a living.Not good man not good.
title: Absolutely only for mosquito lovers.

body: Having visited his brother's property of Lunuganga we were curious to see Bevis Bawa's home and garden. Once again there is a bell to ring, and an entrance fee of 1000 Rupees to pay. We were left to tour the grounds on our own, which was a bit daunting but since it is a relatively small area we did not get lost. It is not particularly well kept but still charming and relaxing. We had a guided tour of the house, which we found very interesting and are pleased we made the effort.
title: Hard to find but worth the effort

body: Worth the 3000 Rupee taxi fair from our hotel to visit these gardens in Bentota .The gardens were laid out with great foresight and vision. The house was modest but brought to life by the man who guided us round. Bevis Bawa was certainly and interesting man. 1000 Rupee entrance fee.
title: Tranquil Gardens

body: Charming gardens, with a variety of plants, and many interesting birds to watch.House also worth a visit, with helpful guide.
title: Interesting gardens and house

body: We knew nothing about Bevis Bawa, although knew about his brother Geoffrey the architect. His garden reflects his life and is fantastic - lots of paths leading to secluded areas where you'll find odd and interesting sculptures (some more interesting than others!). The house is preserved and filled with his possessions. His story is fascinating and Brief Garden gives a glimpse into his hedonistic and self indulgent life. The only problem is finding the place and you are best with a tuk tuk as they know where they're going. Ring the bell and you might even get the current owner to give you the tour.
title: Unmissable and not just for the planting

body: If you are in the area then it is highly advisable to visit this place. More than the legacy of Geoffrey Bawa it is the green landscape and the calm environment that takes over mind and soul!
title: Interesting Visit!

body: This is an absolute gem in benthota. A bit hard to locate but when you get there you'll realize it's worth the trouble. This belonged to the brother of the world renowned architect Geoffrey Bawa. The place is called Brief garden by Bevis Bawa. The place is a 7 acre land with a lot of trees and flowers and beautiful landscape. The entrance ticket should be bought at the gate which will be 300/= for just the garden and 1000/= for both garden and house. This is not a location known by many so it wasn't filled much with people. However the manager, Mr. de Silva said that people can come here for a picnic as well. This is worth the visit if you are an admirer of beautiful landscaping, Sri Lankan history, and architecture. The manager/owner is really friendly. He explained the history behind this while treating us with some refreshments. I'd recommend this to anyone who is travelling to beruwala, benthota side.
title: Wonderful getaway

body: Former Plantation bungalow and gardens named after Bevis Bava's father a well known lawyer of Sri Lanka. It is located inland off Dharga town, no wonder it is secret as there are hardly any signs shown on this very narrow village road. All you need to do is ask any of the locals around here as they all know it. Once you get to the main front gates you have to ring a makeshift bell and an attendant will welcome you. Beautiful gardens with an incredible amount of tropical flowers and trees on narrow footpaths with statues dotted around. You need to spend at least half a day here to soak up the atmosphere. The entrance ticket price includes a pot of tea laid outside in the lawns of the bungalow. Inside the bungalow walls are littered with photographs of some Holywood legends and royalty who have visited the place over the years.
title: No wonder it is a secret in a beautiful location

body: This place is extraordinary. The gardens themselves are a bit smaller than you might think but just take a wander and think what it must have been like in its salad days (Vivian Leigh et al were known to hang out there). Sculptures, hidden spaces, waterfalls... Sure it's a little run down but maybe that's the price paid for not having a gift shop the size of Texas accosting you on the way out. Once you've wandered thru the gardens you will reach the house, a beautiful little structure on the hill, full of books and paintings and sculptures. Each piece is intricate and no doubt holds fascinating stories. Bewa left the property to his head gardener who still lives there. I don't want to give too much away. Go and have yourself a little adventure.
title: Magical

body: There can be little doubt that, in its prime, this house and garden was once very impressive and well-worth a visit. However, it is now very run down and only a short step from becoming ramshackle and overgrown. Still of interest for those who wish to see something of the former colonial lifestyle, but nothing more.
title: DISAPPOINTING

body: Gardens were a bit disappointing, didn't take long to look around.The house itself is very pretty, had loads of questions but the local tour guide only knew how to say "Mr Bawa 2 metres tall!" And that was it. Our tuk tuk driver knew more.Well over priced at 1000 each.
title: Only requires Brief Visit

body: On my last visit to Sri Lanka in October 2015 I had visited the Geoffrey Bawa Garden at Lunuganga (see my separate review) but had no time to visit his brother Bevis's place. So I was able to rectify this on my latest tourAccess is along badly made roads and signage is not great. The garden and house would prove difficult to visit for anyone with mobility problems. The attraction would not be suitable for large groupsNot as expansive as Lunuganga, Brief is more intimate and to my mind contained more colourful and lush planting with some exotic specimens. Within the grounds some impressive stone and art work. The house is also more interesting with an eclectic collection of works (some homo erotic) giving an impression of the bohemian and privileged lifestyle once enjoyed by its occupantsAlthough off the usual tourist trail this was well worth a visit
title: Off the beaten trail

body: We took a Tuk Tuk from the Cinnamon Bey Hotel in Beruwala, 1000rps including a stop at the magnificent Buddist temple en route. Would be very difficult finding this garden without a guide. Attractive gardens with lovely views but the highlight is the bungalow tour with the resident owner explaining everything. Well worth the visit just to see all the artwork and artefacts of a recently decadent by-gone age. Probably a bit boring for youngsters. Well worth the 1000Rp entrance fee.
title: Fascinating visit.

body: Lovely gardens to wander through with sculptures dotted around then guided through the house, ending with a cup of tea! Great views
title: Interesting

body: We visited the Brief Garden just a short distance from hubbub of Bentota. It is a little slice of tranquility. Although the garden is smaller than Lunuganga it is still well worth a visit. We arrived there just as it started to rain but umbrellas were quickly provided. At the end of the tour of the garden before we looked around the house we had an excellent cup of tea with the owner who had inherited the house from Bevis Bawa. Take the chance if you can to make the time for this chat as it is full of interesting information about the history of the house and garden and its creator. Do go along if you have the time.
title: A lovely surprise

body: If you are going to Lunagunga (brother Geoffrey Bawa's weekend retreat) I recommend that you visit Brief in the morning, then have lunch at Lunagunga and go round that garden afterwards. I completely endorse the review by Romeboy which says it all much better than I can. Watch out for the photo of Larry Olivier and Peter Finch, who stayed when they were filming Elephant Walk (wonderful old poster at the Empire Hotel in Kandy!). Very tricky to find - take a driver or a tuk-tuk.
title: Bevis Bawa's retreat in a gloriously decadent and stylish house and garden

body: We went by tut tut which cost approx 1500 rupees, entrance was 1000 rupees, a very interesting place, lovely gardens with little secret corners, all very tropical , ending with a tour of the house with its paintings and artworks, what a time they must have had !!!
title: A real garden in the tropics, a bit of history too

body: Lovely trees and well landscaped with views of river and lake. Guided visit, well informed guide. It takes about 2 hours walking slowly in the the heat
title: Walk in the garden and see the elegant rooms (through the windows)

body: We recommend taking a tuk-tuk there as the directions to the house are minimal. Also, there are many steps (some of them high) and uneven terrain in the grounds and garden, which could be challenging for the elderly or differently-abled. This is were Bevis Bawa retired after his brief career in the army and where he surrounded himself with a bevy of boys, young men, gentlemen and similar masculine companions. While the grounds are nice, we liked the house the most. Beautifully designed, decorated and furnished, it truly reflects Bawa's taste and upbringing. The Picassos, Gauguins and Cocteaus - despite being copies - reminisce of the atmosphere and the erotic fauna that the house enjoyed in the 50s and 60s. Walking in the open-air Roman-style baths in one of the room's private courtyard, we wondered what the darkened and foggy mirror would say if it were ever allowed to tell what it saw!The current resident, the former head gardener to whom Bawa donated the house (!), is doing a good job preserving the house as it was when Bawa died: simple, elegant, decadent, and yet ready for a pool party and music and boys, should the former ghosts decide to visit one night. A magical place indeed.
title: Decadence, Myth, Eros, Art, Still Hang in Colonial House and Grounds - beware of steps

body: Found the location in Lonely Planet guide book. We stopped there on our way from Colombo to Galle. Our driver had difficulty to find the place. Finally we arrived and paid the 1000Rs/p fee. Worth the price! The garden and house are very well maintained. Garden and house are so beautiful and quiet, 1-2 hours visit in this enchanted place
title: a paradise

body: Difficult to find the place as no directions are given. Entrance fee is Rs 1000. Garden is not at all great. Plenty of greenery and quite vast. The colonial bungalow is the highlight. Boring for children. It can be seen within an hour.
title: Nothing great, simple home garden, Nice colonial bungalow

body: We visited the Brief Gardens on the recommendations of the owner of Diya Sisila last January but didn't get a chance to go last year so made a point of going this year.Well it was certainly worth the wait, it was such a tranquil peaceful place to be and it just transported us back to the 1930's. We could just imagine what life would have been like living there in that era. It obviously isn't as it should be as they don't have the money for the upkeep but they are certainly trying to maintain it as best they can with limited funds.Following the many meandering paths lead you to the house which is awash with beautiful works of art and furniture that is now looked after by a wonderful Sri Lankan gentleman and his family. He very kindly gave us a history of Bevis and Geoffrey Bawa and the house and gardens that they created followed by a lovely cup of tea.We absolutely loved this place and will definitely visit again next time we are in Sri Lanka.I understand that the price advertised on Trip Advisor for the entrance fee is 370 rupees however it is now 1000 rupees (£5) but well worth it.......Fabulous.
title: Breathtaking

body: Beautifully designed and maintained natural style garden. Well worth a visit if gardens interest you.The guided tour of the house and information about Bevis Bawa was fascinating and cup of tea very welcome. Apparently the road has recently been improved ,we had no problems visiting by tuk tuk.
title: Beautifully designed and maintained natural style garden

body: The tour around the garden was beautiful if you like to see typical Sri Lankan trees, flowers and buildings. But the most wonderful thing about this visit was the lunch in the garden. We got served twelve different curries, all of them very tasty. We would recommend a trip here, mostly to taste the food.
title: Beautiful garden and the best lunch.

body: Our driver offered to bring us to this garden. We are eternally grateful for this suggestion. The guide seemed a little "annoyed" with the visitors but after showing genuine interest in the house and the life of the Bawa's, he appeared to be a very funny, thoughtful and knowledgeable guide. Loved it!!!
title: Worthwhile and captivating

body: Beautiful grounds, I like the fact that it isn't perfectly manicured - much more natural. 'Brief Garden' is a good name - we toured the grounds in 40 minutes but still worth a visit if you're not coming from far away.
title: Lovely miniature garden paradise

body: I can't believe when people below have written that they think the gardens and home have not been maintained.I strongly recommend you organize seeing this estate. We did Lunuganga too and organized a meal there but didnt organize in enough advance at Brief to dine there but I wish I did. Email on info@briefgarden.com a few days before to do so.We took a proper car / driver to this location as the reviews say it is a rural once you get off the main road. I wouldn't like the idea of rattling around on a tuktuk to get there. It is LKR 1000 (7$USD) and our tour was unguided but at the end, the man who Brief was left to spoke to us a bit about the history so I think you can get more of a proper guided tour and info if you want.The gardens and sculptures are fascinating and I would love to live in the home myself - all the interesting furniture, art work, antiques and books. The Bawa's bohemian sanctuary properties are not to missed if you are near by.
title: Absolutely Must Do

body: Lovely place to visit and stroll through the garden but most interesting part is the house. Fascinating for people interested in architecture and design.
title: Inspiring

body: If you are a fan of out of the box architecture that goes with nature, then it worth paying a visit. The ride to the property takes 15-30 minutes from Aluthgama
title: For nature and architectural fans

body: Even though the garden is designed beautifully it has not maintained properly ...The road leading to the garden from bentota is extremely remote...
title: Nice place but....

body: We visited this place, and cant believe the climate over there. its like Nuwara eliya. beautiful green plants and river by the side. there was a restaurant but its bit expensive.
title: like a paradice

body: It was my dream to visit the world famous Breif Garden- Bentota by Bevis Bava since i were a little girl. Heard about its unique beauty and the the out standing creativity of Bava in planning everything. So after several years of endless dreaming we made our way to visit the so called garden of heaven. It was a very rough route to access and after all the hard traveling of around 2 hours from Galle, we managed to reach Kalavila.We had to take the train,then the bus and finally a tuk tuk. The access road was pathetic and not well managed. it was a terribly hot area. But the management refused to allow us enter. It was very rude how they behaved and how they treated us. Their reason of refusing us was that we were a couple. They insisted not to allow us enter so we had to return back. This was a very pathetic and uncomfortable experience for both of us because we were exhausted after the tiresome journey. If this were their hospitality for two locals, i am very confused how they would treat the foreign visitors who would come there all their way from the motherland. It was indeed a dream killer a terrible place to visit.
title: Breif Garden, a dream killer

body: Visited here on the strength of reviews but left extremely dissapointed. After arriving by Tuk Tuk over some rough terrain which was nice to be out of the hustle of the main roads it cost 1000 rubes to enter. I thought I was in for seeing spectacular gardens but it was generally over grown and the house was a dissapointment too. I have to say in its defence I am not a tourist who is a lover of historical land marks and a couple who were in English who were there at the same time were raving about it - so not for everyone but some yes.
title: Left dissapointed

body: Beautiful gardens and residence with an interesting history. The Brief Garden is a bit off the beaten track, so arrange round-trip transportation. This site is not to be missed if in the Bentota area.
title: Not to be missed when in the Bentota area

body: An interesting place to visit and hear the history surrounding the house and gardens .maybe not the best place when it's raining . The road is a bit on the rough side but a bit of fun .
title: Interesting history lesson

body: The Brief Gardens were built by the the famous Bevis Bawa. It has not been kept up very well but still worth a visit. price is R/1000 per person. A 25 minute ride from Aluthgama.
title: Still has its Bawa charm

body: Brief Gardens are a real treat for anyone that loves a bit of horticulture. Simple masculine layout to the house and gardens alike. I love the fact that the gardens are not manicured to within an inch of there lives and certain areas have a real feel of the wild. Then of course there are the various statues dotted about, that present a real sense of mischief, you will see for yourselves. We had a lovely pot of tea up at the house, but I understand that this is not always available, so we counted ourselves as lucky. A lovely place to wander and soak up the beauty for a couple of hours, maybe longer if you really take time to enjoy it all.
title: Brief visit to Brief

body: A thing of beauty is a joy forever. On condition of maintaining it. And they are doing this very well here. A foundation looks well after the work of world famous architect Bawa. Many secret places and details do discover. We got so intrigued by it that we followed Bawa's trail for a few days, untill we reached his houde and atelier in Colombo. The picture books about him were, alas, too heavy to carry. This is only where he got the inspiration for his magnificent garden: in his brother's one.
title: Expensive ticket but soooo interesting.

body: I did not know a lot about Bevis Bawa before visiting this place and probably would have appreciated it more if I had done more research. The gardens give a hint of the magical place they once were. There was a guide in the house who explained all of the features and the stories behind the artwork. Lovely, but out-of-the-way place to visit.
title: Intriguing

body: The gardens and house are a fascinating insight to Bevis Bawa's life and Sri Lankan culture in general. Some of it unexpected and a delight. The grounds are immaculately kept and full of flowers and birds, whilst the house is preserved in a 'shabby' charm!
title: Charming curiosity!

body: This is a treat of a place if you love gardens. You enter through the bungalow which is a lovely place in itself with its collection of art and wonderful old photographs of Bevis Bawa and some of the famous visitors to the Brief. The garden has quite a mysterious quality to it as you wander along winding paths surrounded by lush plants and occasionally happen upon a seating area in a clearing, or a pool or statue. We visited after a rainstorm which had left the garden a vibrant green and a dripping jungle like atmosphere. The drive there takes you through some beautiful countryside too. Well worth a visit. There is an entrance fee which at the time of writing works about to about £5.
title: Delightful

body: A beautiful and historic garden with an aristocratic story attached to it . An extraordinary secret garden in an unexpected location . well worth a look .
title: A beautiful secret garden.

body: Pleasant,verdant garden. Enjoyed a one hour ramble amongst unexpected water features and overgrown paths;even saw two mongooses at close quarters big colonial house with a bit of history.
title: See how the other half lived.

body: A green and ordered oasis behind an impressive hedge. The walk leads one through the tropical gardens with some interesting plantings of tropical vegetation interspersed with landscaping reminiscent of an Italian garden. The house itself is also of interest and had an unexpected treasure trove of art on the walls. Worth the drive to get there.
title: Worth the drive.

body: Architecturally designed garden and bungalow by Bevis Bawa. The garden is divided in to different stages, right in the center is the bungalow. Many man made Lakes and countless trees makes it the ideal place to relax.Bungalow is designed in a way that air flows without any assistance from technology, feels cool inside. has lot of Antiques. the caretakers will give you a tour around the bungalow explaining how it was designed. The entrance fee is way too much if you ask me. but it is a price to pay if you really want to see it. Last visit 2012
title: Architecture and nature in tandem

body: We took a TukTuk for a day visiting these gardens as part of our excursion. What a beautiful and tranquil place. We were able to wander around at leisure and when visiting inside the house a guide gave us an interesting insight into the history of the owner and his family. I would strongly recommend this place for gardeners and non gardeners alike. Not too expensive either.
title: Tranquil setting

body: Architectural place, nice to visit for relaxation and studying architecture. you will see some endemic plants too.
title: Architectural place

body: A nice garden to stroll around in. The grounds are rather big and there is lots to see. The visit ends with a tour of the house and the art collection of Bevis Bawa. Nice and gives some insight in his life. Loved all the stautues and little ponds and features.
title: Lovely garden with nice collection of statues

body: This was a highlight, what a magnificent short day trip. What was created here is just fantastic, and what a great time it must have been to live in Sri Lanka.
title: Fantastic

body: Make the time to come and see this beautiful garden. Easy to get to and in some ways much more beautiful than Lunaganga. A real treat.
title: Beautiful gardens and house.

body: This really is a wonderful garden and house now owned and run by the previous gardener and his family, who used to tend to the gardens for Mr bevis and his partner. It looks simply sumptuous in the rain and still has that wonderful charm and magic about it. Well done Dan and the de Silva family for continuing to uphold Bevis's legacy.
title: Still as gorgeous as ever.

body: Beautiful grounds to wander through followed by a tour of the house with an informative guide, but wear mosquito repellant otherwise you'll have loads of itchy bites!
title: Beautiful

body: The biggest problem with Brief Garden is the lack of directions both to get to the gardens and once their around the garden itself. Constructed in 1929 and opened to the public 40 years later, not a lot has been done to assist the visitor. Even the toilet located in the garden is a health hazard, certainly not there to be used!
title: Interesting garden with unrealized potential

body: Was a bit of a drive down a narrow road to get hear but once we got there felt it was fully worth the trip. A ticket to view the garden and home of Bewis Bawa costs Rs.1000 per person. There is an ancient bell that needs to be rung to inform that you have arrived. The garden is full of little nooks with seating and abstract sculptures with space for outdoor sports and even dining. The walk up to the main house is amazing with a beautifully landscaped garden. The exterior of the house itself is breathtaking but once you enter you feel transformed into a different era.Antique furniture, quaint sculptures and paintings, great library and inner courtyards simply take your breath away.
title: Beauty of a Bygone Era

body: Such peace and tranquility. We spent the day at Brief, walking along the many paths through luscious greenery and calm waters. Many sculptures and statues placed in the gardens give an insight to Bawa's lifestyle. Highly recommended for a day out.
title: Paradise surrounded by trees, ponds, greenery.

body: Personal tour of the gardens and beautiful house. Entry 1000 rupees which goes towards upkeep. Take a picnic.
title: Peace from a bygone era

body: It was a nightmare to get to the garden. There are no signs and the road is almost non-existent. After a long search we reached the place to find it desolate. We returned utterly disappointed.
title: Horrible access with absolutely no signs to guide you

body: We spent a lovely afternoon here wandering round the neat lawns. An English garden with spectacular exotic flowers. The house is beautiful and the lovely gentleman who showed us round and made our tea brought the house to life with stories of the past. Magical
reviewer_location: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
title: Afternoon tea in a quaint setting

body: hard to find. no signs of indication. charging visitors but unable to see any maintenance. very neglected. Was greeted by a very rude, unfriendly man. visitors are locked in the garden once entered. to get out must ring a bell and wait for him to open gate.Not worth seeing. Waste of money.
title: neglected

body: lovely place, beautiful gardens, full of history, although the house could do with some TLC the art and sculptures are amazing, and not far from Bentota
title: peaceful

body: This garden is in serious need of maintenance. This is a smaller property compared to its bigger cousin Lunaganga, but there are weeds everywhere, the trails are unmarked and the paths slippery with mosses. The guide seemed uninterested and rude. Like Lunaganga, this place has potential to be major tourists attraction, but in serious need of care. Unlike Lungaganga, this is in private hands. The Government should take over this to promote tourism.
title: Need of maintenance

body: Tranquil gardens on a much smaller scale than those of his brother at Lunuganga but worth a visit. There was no guide to walk around and explain everything here but when I reached the houes the guide gave much information about the house, statues, Bevis Bawa's artistic friends and house guests. Very interesting.
title: Tranquil gardens

body: Bevis Bawa may not have had the fame and talent of his brother Geoffrey, but his garden at The Brief is a wonderful exercise of trying to keep the jungle under some control, while letting it be part of it at the same time. Mass plantings of one plant on various locations creates a calmness next to the riot of growth nearby. Good fun to see, lots of work for the maintenance workers!
title: A controlled jungle garden

body: Hidden away inland it is not the easiest of places to find. But it is worth it, not a huge garden but lovely views and interesting house. Peaceful. Bevis bawa was an interesting chap.
title: perfect clearing in the jungle.

body: Brief House is approximately 10 kilometres inland with no public transport so got a tuk tuk ride. The journey after turning off the main road was great, passing through small villages in the countryside as I ventured further inland. Not well signposted but the locals happy to give directions. The entrance is like coming through a secret door into a tropical paradise. The gardens are extensive with large stands of trees and tropical vegetation in a wild layout with artistic follies scattered throughout. Brevis Bawa's house appears to be as he left it, full of amazing artwork with murals on the walls and a splendid one by Donald Friend a renowned Australian artist who came for a week and stayed 5 years. Don' t miss the collection of photos giving an insight into the lifestyleof Bawa and his famous visitors. It was a privilege to chat with the current owner, who was a long term manager for Bawa. He shared so much fascinating information about artwork, history and gardens that enriched my visit. Can only imagine the grand parties!
title: Artistic treasure

body: Lots of grounds to cover. Tour not as good as we hoped. The pet dog knew the tour blindfolded so we followed him.
title: Tranquil

body: well, its interesting - so if you are around do visit, but dont build your day around itthe original owner had special interest hence strange pieces of art, see the picture
title: slightly odd place

body: Loved Bevis Bawa's gardens and house, full of art history and faded glamour. The hospitality we received was simply wonderful, tea and biscuits chatting to the current owner was a real highlight.
title: Must Do !

body: Definitely worth leaving the beach for a couple of hours to visit this hidden gem. Bevis Bawa's garden and house are stunning and incredibly well kept. One could spend hours inspecting the garden alone. The house has been left as it was when he lived there. One can't help wandering about the crazy parties which must have gone on there!
title: The secret garden

body: if you are passionate about landscaping, architecture, this is a place that you need to see. But if you are not really interested about these, you will not finding anything much interesting. if you are going there via Southern highway, please don't follow the road that google maps shows (via road to Sri Sudarmarama temple rd) - instead go via Aluthgama-Mathugama- Yatidola road which is more closer to Darga town- this is a better road. this place has comparatively expensive entry fee (for locals also - Rs. 350 for garden and Rs. 1000 if you want to see both garden and house). I rather recommended both house and garden option. don't miss to talk to caretaker in case you are visiting the house. He guide you through the house and tell you lot about history. also make sure that you see following in the house,old photo collection of bevis bawa (about 10),painting that brief whole Sri Lankathree painting on the walls of same corridor Court yard with out door bathing area anyway don't expect too much from the garden. it had been a private garden of a house, not a botanical garden.
title: if you are passionate about landscaping, don's miss this

body: This house and garden is lovely, though the prudish might be taken aback by some of the sculptures. We were offered tea - nothing could be more perfect.
title: Tea in paradise

body: Of all the experiences in Sri Lanka this was our number one. Our party of four took 2 tuk tuks to the house of this larger than life Sri Lankan [6ft 7 inches} The house id s full of artwork and treasures and our guide worked for Bevis so new so much. The gardens are beautifully landscaped, Tea on the lawn mad the vist perfect.
title: An amazing oasis of beauty

body: Very interesting garden and house, well worth a visit and not crowded.Intereting to compare eith other Bawa buildings such as The Gsllery cafe in Colombo.
title: Design

body: What a beautiful place to visit its a short tuk tuk ride to these lovely gardens and house with a interesting story now left to the staff who cared for the owner until his death you can then visit a nearby temple and see the everyday life of Sri Lanka people en-route
title: Peaceful birdsong

body: Down some very narrow rough roads (with no signs pointing the way), this is a great way to spend an hour or so away from the beach. The house and grounds are beautiful – and an inspiration for landscaping back at home. Don’t expect formal gardens or placards identifying plants – but rather just a nice place to explore and fantasize about escaping everyday world and moving to a garden paradise in the middle of no where yourself.
title: Tucked away gem

body: Geoffrey Bawa was a very important architect in Sri Lanka. This house and garden developed some of his ideas on light space and shape and vistas (and his sense of humour) as well as displaying some of the art he collected or commissioned by a range of artists and sculptors
title: House and garden designed by Geoffrey Bawa for his brother

body: It is located way too much in the interiors . If you are in self drive with gps then I will not suggest going there. After much meandering I found a rickshaw who asked me to follow him to the gardens otherwise I would have got lost . The entry charges are thousand rupees
title: Not worth the effort

body: Lanscaping and the design was good. They charge a lot to visit the place but I think they can maintain the garden more than that. Lots of mosquitos and they could have done the needful. Unfriendly gate keeper.
title: Expected more

body: Unspoilt full of birds. A guided tour around the villa with a very interesting history. Well worth a visit
title: Beautiful

body: We really enjoyed the Bevis Bawa Garden, it is stunning and beautiful, we were amazed by ist varaiety of plants and stautes/figures. A must see see if you like nature.
title: Lovely Garden , a must see if your close to Beruwela!

body: I thought it is a bit over rated. Could be maintained better for a fee of one thousand rupees. But we had an excellent cup of Sri Lankan tea!!
title: Brief Garden

body: Beautiful garden and house with unusual plants, especially black flower is wonderful.For a relatively short period of time and small fee we saw a delightful garden and house created by Sri Lankan landscape architect Bevis Bawa.Enjoyment and relaxation in melt of nature and human mind.
title: Nice garden and house

body: Very atmospheric and well worth a visit. The gardens are well cared for and very interesting. Watch out for the mongoose,......
title: Don't miss it!

body: Just a short ride in a tuk-tuk from our hotel and well worth it..a couple of hours is enough to take in the beautiful gardens and house. Lots of flowers and birds and a free cuppa at the end of the tour.
title: Lovely house and gardens

body: Disapointed with the gardens. Not enough information or even a map. House was interesting but the whole thing was not worth the entry fee.
title: Disapointing

body: Lovely large tranquil gardens but the house is very interesting. it belonged to the architect and designer Bevis Bawa, a homosexual who was the darling of the Hollywood crowd in the 50's. Beautifully deigned spacious rooms, he died without children and left the house and over 24 acres to his staff,The Butler, who now owns the house will show you around.
title: Designers and architects home

body: We took a tuk tuk from our guest house in Bentota - approx. 25 mins drive each way - paid rps 1200. The drive was interesting in itself, but then the gardens and house was amazing. We were left to wander alone around the gardens then given a guided tour of the house and its' history. Bevis Bawa had the most incredible life and this is portrayed in his former home. Make sure you see the outdoor shower and the moon gate too.
title: Well worth making a trip

body: The present owner explained how the house and gardens came about, they form a quiet and tranquil setting. Was used as a emergency shelter for 200 tourist in 2004 after the Tsunami. Owner refused a large compensation sum from the tourist industry but donated it to the town to pay for scholarship for local students.
title: Steeped in History

body: Beautiful gardens with many lovely flowers and plants. We even got to see a group of monkeys high in the trees feeding on fruits. It is well worth a visit if you like gardens and tranquil surroundings.
title: Tranquility guaranteed

body: Worth the trip to see this amazing estate and house. The gardens and paths are charming and the house a perfect setting in the climate. Entry is 1000 Sri Lankan Rupees per person and worth it. We took a Tuk-Tuk there and that is the best way to get around.
title: What a delightful place

body: It's a beautifully laid out garden, though the entrance fee is steep (SLR 1000 per person). And for the price one doesn't even get a guide to walk along and point out the sights or even give some history of the garden. Visitors are left to figure things out for themselves.
title: Beautiful garden but not enough details for visitors

body: Beautiful and interesting place,filled with amazing works of art of the Bawa and his friends. The house itself is an architectural pearl. The gardens are inspiring. we all loved the place. Worth a visit if you stay in Bentota or Beruwela area. A half an hour with a three wheeler which in itself is a lovely experience. Only downside is the high entrance fee, in sri-lankan terms of course. 100 rup. Per person.
title: Beautiful place

body: The garden and the house are very nice and the guide gives you a great introduction to the life of Bevis Bawa and the estate. He was perfectly speaking english and german and made the tour very interesting. We love the estate!
title: A must!

body: The beautiful expanse of greenery... Garden is manicured yet so wild in places to keep the natural charm alive.. We fell in love with this romantic garden and the family who welcomed us there. A must visit for all nature gazing lovers.
title: Did not want to leave Brief Garden!

body: We really enjoyed our two hour visit, especially as we shared tea with the charming owner. He could not have been more patient and informative about the house, garden and the Bawa family. The garden in a carefully choreographed "jungle" with some beautiful (and sometimes quirky) architectural features and ornaments. The collection of photographs and paintings in the house - which is light and spacious - helped turn the clock back to its heyday. A really memorable trip, just 1000 rupees waiting tuk tuk from the coast.
title: Garden of delights

body: I found the house and garden moderately interesting, but the real "wow" was the range of birds that could be seen (and photographed). This is a "must" for bird enthusiasts: allow a half day and bring your binoculars and long lens!One of the best locations for birds that I visited during my entire tour.
title: Well worthwhile. Fantastic for birds.

body: I had read about these gardens and had a half day to spare so went along.The garden is beautiful. The flowers and exotic plants were fascinating. I heard a variety of birds and enjoyed searching for sight of them.I must say however. The house gave me the creeps and I couldn't applaud the statues and paintings. I would not have wanted my son to go there as a child or young man shall we say.Definitely worth a visit though.
title: first visit to brief garden

body: might be an interesting walk around the gardens if you have company and fancy a change of scene .. interesting take on colonisation and creating a space where you can live as you please .. surreally, there is a Picasso in the somewhat indiscriminate art collection
title: hmm

body: An unexpected garden. Full of quirky ideas. So lush and green. The wife of the owner is a lovely lady and knows so much about the history of the house and the family that formerly owned it. The photos on the walls show many film stars from bygone times. Sit and look at the view from the terrace. It is hard to leave it. In the garden are colourful birds and monkeys. At every twist and turn in the garden there is something new to look at.Don't miss this garden!
title: Such a Green & Peaceful Place

body: this was the best thing we did on our visit, the house and gardens are such a pleasant surprise and very interesting too, not very big so you can do it all in an hour but you wouldnt want to eave the cool and beautiful house once youre there
title: shangrila

body: This place is hard to find. The turn from the main road is easily missed but press on as it is worth the look. The gardens are luxurious and it has a real kept, unkept look and feel. Fantastic entrance to the house from the car park. The house is a classic open style Bawa house. Must have been great in it's halcyon days full of the rich and famous!
title: Lovely garden and house

body: Was a lovely experience. Every turn, every bend in the path was interesting - so many many plants. Very beautifully laid out garden. You can spend ages in this place without getting tired - if you are a nature lover. Sitting down to have some tea and biscuits in the Bawa home was also a treat. If they do up this house and let out the rooms, then this is a must stay place.
title: Walk through Brief Garden

body: What a fantastic look into the past. The gardens were laid out with great foresight and vision. Though the house was modest, one can only imagine heady lifestyle enjoyed by the Bawa clan. Well worth a visit
title: Brief Gardens

body: If you are open minded, like something truly out of the ordinary and off the beaten tourist track, then this is definitely for you. Take a tuk tuk for a magic ride into the past and visit the Brief Garden to discover how it was to live a decidedly debauched lifestyle in the colonial days leading up to Ceylon's independance.In the middle of a forest you come upon stunning landscaped gardens supporting a myriad of trees,plants,flowers and wildlife to soak in. You then arrive at the sparse but beautiful house, full of impressive paintings and photographs of a bygone age. To cap it all there is some pretty dubious but nevertheless eye catching sculptures to be studied! The 1000 rupee entrance fee is quite high for Sri lanka but certainly, from our point of view, worth every rupee.Before going it is worth looking up the history of Bevis & Geoffrey Bawa to give you some idea of what there is in store for you. A wonderful experience.
title: Divine Decadence

body: An interesting taste of old colonial living. Nice shady walks amongst the trees (beware mosquitos) stumbling upon oddities here and there. Then an interesting tour of the house and art and finally a wonderful cup of tea on the shaded terrace. Very enjoyable interlude.
title: Charming, Quirky & Tranquil

body: Small gardens with weird history and plenty of artwork. Staff were lovely. p.s WEAR LOTS OF BITE CREAM
title: Interesitng but strange

body: We were more like that tour. very nice and lovely place. calm & relax. we saw nice trees and herbal plant.
title: Very good village tour

body: Beautiful gardens but research the owner and his past first!? The atmosphere and artwork in the house were strange.
title: Umm....

body: Make no mistake, Brief Garden is off the beaten path. You will want to investigate whether it is worth the trouble to get there. Garden aficionados might want to visit, but don't take a rickshaw. Too, the pedophilia element surrounding Bevis Bawa adds another dimension to the question of visiting. The Rs 1000 admission fee is a bit over priced.
title: Likely not worth your trouble

body: Wasn't expecting such magical gardens hidden away. Well worth visiting to take in the gardens and architecture, even if you're not a buff.
title: Hidden treasure

body: Interesting way to spend a couple of hours wandering around the lovely grounds and viewing the house.
title: Brief Garden

body: Excellent and lovely garden, great welcome from Dooland and his wife. Well manicured garden in a peaceful location!Must see if you are around Beruwala area.
title: Lovely

body: Bevis Bawa had a great eye for design as did his boyfriend Donald. The garden and house make an interesting tour with lots of take home ideas. Yes the man was gay and young Sri Lankan males were involved but to downgrade this place because of the sexual orientation of the owner somewhat misses the point. The whole area reflects his sensitivity, sensuality and imagination and unlike his brother's property, Lunaganga, you can see inside the house as well. You may not admire the man but you must admire his talent.
title: Worth a visit for lovers of good and timeless design.

body: OK, so the house and gardens are presentable. The moon gate is interesting, but that's where it stops.Make no mistake, this place reeks of paedophilia. Everything about it, from the "special" places and hidey-holes in the gardens where young boys where taken, to the phallic statues and sad photographic portraits of young boys.Bawa, Donald Friend and their cronies should be remembered for what they were.
title: Nice garden, shameful history

body: Wonderful garden and house is full of interesting art work. Fascinating contrast to Lunagunga. A must for Bawa fans.
title: A must for Bawa fans

body: A bit of a hike going there and our driver was not overly keen since it was a small dirt road but we loved wandering around the garden snapping away at the different vistas and 'rooms', mosquitoes are definitely loving seeing tourists there but manageable. As for the house, the 'keeper' was not overly enthusiastic in his commentary but we enjoyed it anyway...Mr Bawa's was obviously was a bit of an eccentric who loved to be surrounded by beautiful things and people butif the sight of a statue of a male naked & a few lascivious pictures are too much for you...don't bother (then don't bother with many other parts of the world, italy, greece, india... and BTW don't bother with art all together !)
title: pretty garden and very comfortable experience

body: The garden was beautiful and we had a very pleasant stroll through the jungle like growth. The tour of the house spoiled the experience for us, however, as the hallway exiting the house showcased paintings and photographs that implied that Bawa's boy servants were victims of pedophilia. These acts should never be condoned, let alone celebrated, and we remain shocked that this hasn't come up in previous reviews or guidebook write-ups about the place. While the gardens were quite pretty, we struggle to recommend visiting Brief Gardens for these reasons and the chilling atmosphere that burdens many areas of the property.
title: Pretty gardens, but a very uncomfortable experience overall

body: We chose this place based on Tripadvisor number 1 rating, when we arrived we had to ask to know our way there.entrance fee is 1000 LRSthe attraction is composed of Bevis Bawa's ( a Srilankan Artist) garden which he desined himself and his home, he died in 1993 hi house has some of his paintings and a lot of other artists contributionsif you are an artist then this is a place for you.if you aren't into art then I think you will get a bit bored like we did.
title: Below our expectations

body: This was a very relaxing spot. It shows you dont need fancy flowers or exotic ornaments. The placement of trees and the care taken with the garden planning shows what a talented person Bevis was
title: Shows what great planning can do with little

body: we went there and we liked a lot!It's a very nice place, with a nice tropical garden. We went there with a Tuk-tuk from Bentota, all the drivers that we asked for a price know this place.Personally I think it's a nice landscape garden topped with a nice colonial house. But nothing to compare with his brother Geoffrey Bawa's house in Lunuganga. That all single detail are there for some reason.
title: very nice

body: Brief Gardens is a masterpiece of landscaping. I could have spent all day here, observing the play of light and shadow in the changing daylight. It is also a wonderful opportunity for photography. A single visit will hardly do it justice. This was my second visit and I shall certainly return in another season.
title: A Garden for Connoisseurs - a Work of Art

body: We were taken by tuk tuk from our hotel by a driver who obviously knew his way, but I could easily see why it might be difficult to find - as other reviewers have stated. Having read previous reviews, I doused myself in deet before arriving! However, within minutes of getting there, I had been bitten numerous times. I reapplied copious amounts of repellent whilst there, which appeared to stop further bites. I liked the serenity of the garden, but felt I was hurrying through, to ensure I didn't get bitten again. There wasn't much in bloom, but I managed a few interesting photos. The house was spartan, but had a rather nice, colonial feel about it. Normally, apparently, there is a gentle breeze wafting through, but on the day we were there it was stifling. I enjoyed the photo collection and in particular, the lovely, natural photo of Vivien Leigh and Laurence Olivier. The history of some of the artefacts in the house was explained, however, nothing was mentioned of the garden. We were not offered any refreshments and if I'm honest, I wasn't disappointed to leave.
title: A brief visit!

body: Very cool and almost like an English garden - we particularly liked the cascade run of water down the lawn from the top by the house. Tea and lemon puff biscuits were provided after the tour of the garden - a nice touch. Interesting to hear the history of the house and gardens and see the old photos of past visitors.
title: Interesting garden

body: Interesting but slightly disappointing...We expected it to be more colourful from what we'd read about it.
title: Brief Garden

body: This was a great visit! Our driver took us there early in the day. It is not very easy to find, it is a hidden gem in the middle of lash trees and plantations. The tour guide is great! We got to know that the place is full of charm and stories to share. The paintings on the wall are really touching. The one of Bevis Bawa in his very late days with the boy with his arm around him is breath-taking, and leaves you with so much to think about. So much charm and so many stories in the house. The building itself is not a palace, but the garden is something to tell about. We set in the garden at the end of the tour, and enjoyed a cup of tea, and let the whole place sink in with us. It is an experience not to be missed! A very moving experience...
title: A place full of atmosphere

body: It's not easy to find Brief Garden as the signs have disappeared recently so suggest that you take a tuk-tuk. It was the home of the artist Bevis Bawa, the very well connected younger brother of Geoffrey Bawa who was a renowned architect. The extensive gardens are truly wonderful and beautifully kept. It's a real tropical paradise with so much to see - all types of trees, shrubs, flowers, water features, pathways, statues, pots etc - and a real pleasure to amble around. Included in the entrance fee is a guided tour of the house, which is very interesting. It is rumoured locally that Bevis Bawa was a well endowed gentleman and there are a number of images and sculptures possibly based on him, of naked men with large attributes, which may make some visitors blush!
title: Beautiful!

body: This is a beautiful and serene place to visit. Set amid a coconut plantation, Brief Garden is lush and aesthetically pleasing. The caretaker is knowledgeable and offers insights into the history of the garden and house. The gardens are divided into outdoor rooms revealing Bawa's sense of style and sense of humor.We found the place with difficulty but felt the trek was worth it.
title: Serenity

body: It was clean and always well kept, pool was clear and lovely and the whole thing was private and safe
title: Beautiful Garden

body: Brief Gardens are a 'must see' for anybody visiting the Beruwela - Aluthgama - Bentota area. Although somewhat overgrown now, the gardens still show traces of their original grandeur, and the bird life is wonderful. The bungalow and it's associated art works are splendid, and give some impression of the colonial lifestyle in Sri Lanka fourty or more years ago.Overall, don't miss it!
title: A hidden Gem in the Jungle

body: The garden is relatively small, but divided into different 'rooms' by screens of shrubbery and trees, as well as by stone steps and a series of different levels. There is a barbecue area, several ponds, a cascade (which was dry during our visit) and shady benches to sit on and chill out. The owner of the house welcomed us personally and gave us tea and biscuits in the courtyard, followed by a tour of the house, with its amazing collection of art (particularly gay art) and comic pieces, as well as its fascinating history. It's a quirky, unique attraction and you are either going to love it or hate it. It's also a long way from the main road, and the only practical way to get there is by tuc-tuc or motorbike. I think you'll find it worth the effort though. I suggest you take a picnic and a good book and make a laid back day of it.
title: Well worth a look

body: I really enjoyed my visit to Brief garden. It's beautifully designed offering lots of interesting little areas, lovely views, and several interesting water features. The house is also really attractive, with interesting artwork. The gardens are not mobbed by tourists which made the experience more pleasurable.
title: Loved it!

body: I had a few hours to kill in Bentota, waiting for a train back to Colombo, after a trip around the South coast. A Tuk Tuk driver helped me at the station with my enquiry, and then tried to persuade me to visit the gardens. By this time in my trip I was tired, and to say the least, rather jaded in my dealings with Tuk Tuk drivers. Because of his appearance and manner (very smart and polite) I decided to go. body: We visited Brief Garden while staying at Lunuganga. If you can swing it, I would say it is worth seeing both (Lunuganga should be reserved well in advance, phone ahead for Brief). Either one is a welcome reprieve if you've been spending too much time on Bentota's beaches. (I know, not possible for some.)If you do manage to see both gardens, the comparisons will be inevitable. As you may hear, both Bawa brothers were talented but with differences in their approach. It should be noted that (the older) Bevis' Brief Garden was first and was the precursor to inspire Geoffrey's Lunuganga, if not eventually spurring Geoffrey's entire architectural career. And the two properties are very different to begin with. Brief is inbound within the jungle, while Lunuganga is larger with a lake bordering its opposite ends. The experience of Brief is intimate in size, the garden is organized by designated paths with lushly dense tropical foliage. Following these paths, you happen upon sudden openings and clearances that are humanly scaled - almost like garden "rooms". Some of these open spaces might have a water feature, formal stairs, or spaces sized for activities. The feeling of the garden as "rooms" is more clearly evident in the garden spaces behind the house (such as the outdoor shower area) that the tour guide will take you through. Lunuganga is more pastoral in comparison. Indeed, Geoffrey kept cows on it (still there) that maintained its legal status as agricultural land. There is a spatial flow to the rolling hills and stepped plateaus that contrast to the jungle walkways of Brief. Lunuganga is often cited as one of the factors that ultimately led Geoffrey to get formal architectural training. This may add to the sense that Lunuganga is the work of someone more concerned with space. As far as I can tell, Bevis designed his garden primarily as an enthusiast.I am surprised that few if any comments on TA thus far make mention of what appeared to be Bevis' undeniably overt orientation. In one sense, it should not matter. Yet, I think it provides a fascinating angle from which one can reflect on the brothers and their relationships to their gardens and the world. There are records which suggest Geoffrey may have also veered this way, although they are only inferences, as he did not openly project this image as his brother did.Entering Brief Garden, you feel like you are allowed into Bevis' private world. Homo-eroticism abounds - some blatantly obvious, some quite suggestive, some with a touch of cheeky humour. It reads as a place where he was free to let loose and enjoy life on his own terms without abandon. Viewed in this light, outdoor spaces which are "intimately scaled" take on a further dimension. (Something happening behind those moving bushes?)Likewise, Lunuganga is an interesting documentation of Geoffrey's world. You could almost chart his career as an architect in parallel to its evolution. While Brief seemed somewhat of an inner sanctum, Lunuganga had an expansiveness to it where one did not necessarily "hide" so-to-speak. (There are plenty of physical hiding "spots" but I'm referring more to the mentality.) For example, the male sculptures on display at Lunuganga are significantly more demure in posture - classical rather than wildly expressive. Was this the influence of English propriety alongside English landscape design? Was he acting in accordance with the etiquette expected of someone of his growing renown? Or was Bevis so forwardly extravagant it makes us pale in our moralities?
title: Overt suggestiveness?

body: Finding Brief is not easy, as testified by other reviewers, but every uncertain turn on the ever narrowing roads is rewarded from the moment you walk through the arched gate. The 1000 rupee entrance fee (which helps to maintain the gardens to the traditional standard established under Bevis Bawa) is a tourist bargain. We were free to roam at our leisure and spent nearly 3 hours exploring the gardens and house. The tea spontaneously provided was an unexpected and lovely bonus, as was the tour of the house and historic features. As Australians, we were especially interested in the sculptures and art work of Donald Friend who lived at Brief for several years. His mural of Sri Lankan life, painted on the wall of the main room, was fascinating. The wonderful hospitality of the current owners, the de Silva family, who have enjoyed a long connection to Brief dating back to the Bawa era, the extraordinary beauty and layoutvof the gardens and the tranquility of the setting made Brief the most memorable experience of our Sri Lankan trip. Better signposting and promotion would encourage more visitors I am sure.
title: Persistence rewarded, multifold

body: As an antidote to the hedonistic beaches of southern Sri Lanka, we decided to go inland and explore the attractions that lay within. A visit to the Brief Garden associated with Bevis Bawa (1909-1992) older brother of the more famous Geoffrey Bawa, the renowned architecht,seemed to be just what the doctor ordered. The road trip to the location once one left the main Galle Road at Bentota and traversing narrow rural roads and ups and downs was itself a challenge as there was virtually no signposting. When we finally reached it, the imposing entrance to Brief ( named after the association with lawyers holding briefs)with its ivy covered walls and cement sculptures standing guard over the iron gate was startling.Another shock was the steep entrance fees - Rs 1000SLK per head - which was collected at the door after which we were sheperded into the gardens to find our way about while an earlier Sunday meeting of a local association concluded its tea party.The gardens are the real star of the show, and despite the size having been reduced to just five acres, one could visualise the arboreal grandeur that must have existed in its full majesty.A botanist-guide who knew the trees and the manner in which they came to be would have been appreciated. We finally were admitted to the main house - just about a hour to closing time - and got a rather canned conducted tour where the guide repeated himself several times. The architecture and the imprint of Barbara Sansoni and Donald Friend,the Australian artist during his five-year stay there in the 1950s are absorbing to explore,The sculptures , paintings, courtyards, open air showers and fountains all made their own quiet statements.One could have lingered more but closing hour beckoned and a cuppatea - which sadly never came - would have befitted the admission ticket and the host.

body: I'd never heard of Bawa before this trip, but staying in a property he designed I was interested to see where he used to live. title: Great excursion from Bentota
body: If staying in Bentota for any length of time then this is a very pleasant half day excursion. You enter the grounds and are told to wander around the gardens. These are extensive and rather wild but very interesting with lots of shade and pleasant places to sit and enjoy. When you are ready you are taken for a tour of part of the house. Again very interesting and being served tea on the veranda by the owner is quite entertaining. Several erotic statues around the gardens add interest - most unusual.

title: Just another exciting place near Bentota!

title: A lovely way to spend a morning in Bentota
body: A 20 minute drive in a three wheeler takes you to the Brief Garden. The drive itself is interesting as it takes you off the beaten track. The Brief Garden and House are fascinating, and we were served a lovely cup of tea at the end of our tour.

title: A Brief and memorable diversion
body: We had already visited Lunuganga, the nearby gardens and home of Geoffrey Bawa, before we came to Brief, the home and gardens of his older brother, Bevis.Whilst not as famous, nor as vast as Lunuganga, Brief is an interesting place to visit if you wish to get an insight of the lifestyle of the well-heeled Sri Lankan demi-monde.The home itself is a beautiful old plantation house that Bevis Bawa improved and still contains beautiful antiques, fascinating old photographs and some important artworks - most particularly a wonderful (albeit somewhat time ravaged) mural by the Australian artist Donald Friend, who came to visit Brief for a week and stayed for 5 years. When you see the gardens you can understand why. Brief may not be as grand as Lunuganga, but it is equally as likeable and the staff member who showed us around the house was extremely knowledgable and generous with his time.

title: Interesting visit, excellent English speaking guide
body: We went on a dull, damp. day and were bitten badly by Mosquitos. You were left to wander around the gardens at your leisure and then we had a tour of the house with an excellent speaking guide. The history of the place and Bevis Bawa's life were really interesting. We were served tea before we left which was a lovely touch. However there is no comparison to the magnificent gardens of his brother Geoffrey Bawa.
